title: Correct what Stranded means: not a gateway failure, and the preimage does not recover it
description:
Correct what `Stranded` is documented to mean, in code, ledger text, tests, and the runbook.

## Why this is P1

Not because anything behaves wrongly -- nothing does -- but because the wrong description actively
misleads, and has already demonstrably done so. During the 2026-08-01 analysis it led to a proposal
to build preimage-recovery tooling that could not have recovered anything, caught only because
someone asked why it was needed. A wrong explanation of a money state reproduces itself faster than
it gets checked: the exact stale phrases now appear at 17 sites across 9 tracked files.

## What this bead asserts -- and deliberately does NOT

Three independent adversarial audits of the FIRST drafts of this bead each found a false protocol
claim in the causal story it tried to tell (that forfeit can never strand; that a receive `Failure`
proves the contract was claimed; that a same-seed clone alone can steal the claim). The state has
NEVER been observed in production. That track record is itself the finding: an exhaustive causal
taxonomy of an unobserved state does not survive contact with the protocol, and a code comment is
the worst place to keep one.

So this bead corrects the FALSE claims and stops there. It does NOT establish a complete cause
list. Anything it says about causes is explicitly a non-exhaustive operator aid living in the
runbook, not an invariant in a doc comment.

**What is solidly established (survived all three audits, verified at the pin `72b1e5be`,
wallet-fedimint/Cargo.toml:20):**

- **A misbehaving gateway alone cannot strand a move.** A's send reaches `Success` only against a
  preimage verified against the outgoing contract (`lnv2-client/send_sm.rs:208-211`,
  `lnv2-common/contracts.rs:186-191`), or via A's guardians' `await_preimage`, populated only on a
  verified claim (`lnv2-server/lib.rs:465-476`). B's preimage is derived CLIENT-side as
  `sha256(sha256(ECDH-tweak))` (`lnv2-client/lib.rs:881-889`) and never transmitted; the only copy
  leaving the client is threshold-encrypted to B's guardians (`lnv2-common/contracts.rs:84-89`).
  The gateway holds ciphertext it cannot open.
- **The preimage is NOT the recovery instrument.** It claims A's OUTGOING contract, and a
  send-`Success` means that contract has already been claimed or is claimable by the party holding
  the preimage; spending it is additionally authorised to `claim_pk` (`lnv2-server/lib.rs:465-476`),
  not by the preimage alone. Nothing about it credits B. Where recovery is possible at all the
  instrument is B's claim material (`contract`, `claim_keypair`, `agg_decryption_key`), which the
  SDK persists in `ReceiveSMCommon` (`lnv2-client/receive_sm.rs:35-40`).
- **Forfeit NORMALLY refunds, but "never strands" is FALSE.** The gateway's cancel signature drives
  an immediate refund (`lnv2-client/send_sm.rs:238-266`, `lnv2-server/lib.rs:485-491`) -> normally
  `MovePhase::Refunded`. BUT if the gateway incorrectly claimed the outgoing contract and the refund
  transaction is therefore rejected, the SDK re-checks `await_preimage` and PROMOTES the leg to
  send-`Success` (`lnv2-client/lib.rs:705-725`). That send-Success can then meet a non-claimed
  receive and land in `Stranded`. Document the normal outcome AND this race; do not write "never".
- **A receive `Failure` proves very little.** It is yielded whenever `await_primary_module_outputs`
  fails (`lnv2-client/lib.rs:1049-1053`), which collapses two structurally different mint states
  (`mint-client/src/output.rs:53-71`, `mint-client/src/lib.rs:1528-1534`): `Aborted` (the containing
  transaction was REJECTED -- nothing claimed) and `Failed` (accepted, then issuance failed). It
  therefore does NOT prove the contract was claimed, does NOT prove funds reached B's mint, and
  does NOT exclude a malicious federation -- `output.rs:68-71` says `Failed` "should never happen
  with a honest federation and bug-free code". The honest operator statement is
  **"not proven lost, and not proven recoverable"**, with the uncertainty stated.
- **A second claimant needs more than the seed.** lnv2 has `type Backup = NoModuleBackup`
  (`lnv2-client/lib.rs:329`) and starts a receive SM only when given the specific randomized
  contract (`:964-994`), so a seed-only recovery does NOT resume an in-flight receive. Another
  claimant requires duplicated in-flight client state (a copied data directory, a second daemon on
  the same disk) or explicit access to the contract and claim material. This remains worth checking
  first because it is cheap to rule out and severe if true -- but it is a HYPOTHESIS, not a
  measurement, and "same seed" alone is not sufficient to cause it. Note also that a prior claimant
  is one route INTO the rejected-transaction/`Aborted` class above, not a separate parallel cause;
  do not present them as independent.

## Required changes

1. `wallet-fedimint/src/move_protocol.rs:21-26`: rewrite the `Stranded` doc comment. Keep it
   CONCISE and invariant-shaped -- what observation produces `Stranded` (send settled, receive
   terminal non-claim), what CANNOT be inferred from it (not a gateway fault; not proof of loss;
   not proof of malice), that the preimage does not recover it, and a pointer to the runbook as the
   canonical operator account. Do NOT embed a cause list here: that is the drift-prone thing this
   bead exists to remove.
2. `wallet-fedimint/src/executor.rs:2020-2029` (`stranded_outcome` and its doc comment): the
   message ends "payment preimage saved on the move record" and the comment calls the preimage "the
   durable recovery artifact". Both send an operator after an artifact that cannot help.
   **HARD CONSTRAINT: the leading substring "send settled but receive was not credited" is the
   anchor the runbook's daily stranded check greps for** (docs/real-sats-pilot-runbook.md:121).
   Either keep that substring byte-identical or update the runbook grep in the SAME change.
3. `wallet-fedimint/src/executor.rs:1564`: the inline "(the misbehaving-gateway T4 case)" comment.
4. Tests that assert the stale wording -- these are string-expectation updates, not behaviour
   changes: `executor.rs:3105`, `:3113` (the fabricated `"forfeited"` input at `:3109`), `:3123`,
   `:3157`, and the byte-for-byte ledger fixture at `wallet-fedimint/tests/probe_runtime.rs:708`.
   Replace the fabricated input with the only receive-failure string this wallet can produce, minted
   at `multi_client.rs:1429-1431`. (`"forfeited"` is not entirely absent from the pin -- it occurs
   once in a test doc comment, `lnv2-tests/bin/tests.rs:426` -- but no code path produces it as a
   receive-failure string.)
5. `wallet-fedimint/src/multi_client.rs:1429-1431`: the only receive-failure string the wallet can
   produce copies the SDK's understated "programming error or malicious federation" wording and
   omits the mint-leg cases entirely.
6. `docs/real-sats-pilot-runbook.md:162-179` (stranded incident entry): preserving the data
   directory is still right; the REASON and the next step are wrong. This entry becomes the
   canonical operator account: what cannot be inferred, "not proven lost / not proven recoverable",
   and "check whether another wallet instance is or was running against this data directory" as the
   FIRST diagnostic -- framed as cheapest-to-rule-out, not as the established cause.
7. Live docs that repeat the claim: `docs/phase4-implementation-spec.md:119, 131, 138, 148, 668`
   (authoritative -- `operation-history-spec.md` says the impl spec wins), `docs/roadmap-to-v1.md:78`,
   `docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md:234-238`,
   `docs/adr/0028-web-frontend-localhost-sidecar-session-auth.md:89-93`, and bead `br-5om`.
8. Do NOT edit `docs/archive/**`. Those are historical snapshots of what was believed at the time
   (`integration-phase-plan.md:111`, `phase1-implementation-spec.md:380,389`,
   `2026-07-05-fresh-eyes-review.md:289`); rewriting them falsifies the record.

## Tests

- The corrected stranded tests (`settle_after_send_strands_on_terminal_non_claim`, executor.rs:3095,
  and `successful_send_then_terminal_failed_receive_strands_with_preimage`, executor.rs:3118 --
  note the latter's NAME also encodes the stale framing) use a receive-failure string the SDK can
  actually produce, and still map to `Stranded`.
- A test pins the ledger anchor substring the runbook greps for, so a future reword cannot silently
  break the daily check. Name the runbook in the test's comment.
- Behaviour is unchanged: no state-machine edit, no phase-set edit, no change to when `Stranded` is
  entered. Only descriptions, one fabricated test input, and the expectation strings that quote it.

## Scope guard

Do NOT change the state machine, the phase set, or when `Stranded` is entered. Do NOT build
preimage-extraction or recovery tooling: the preimage cannot recover a stranded move. Do NOT remove
the `Stranded` phase; it remains correct defensive modelling. Do NOT re-introduce an exhaustive
cause list into a code comment. Greenfield repo: no compatibility shims.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] MECHANICAL: `git grep -n -e "misbehaving-gateway" -e "payment proof saved" -e "preimage saved"
      -e "durable recovery artifact" -- '*.rs' 'docs/**' ':!docs/archive'` returns ZERO hits.
      (Scoped deliberately: `.beads/` is excluded because this bead's own text quotes the phrases,
      and `docs/archive/**` is excluded per required change 8.)
- [ ] The `Stranded` doc comment states the invariant and points to the runbook, and contains no
      enumerated cause list.
- [ ] No code comment, ledger string, live doc, ADR, or bead describes `Stranded` as caused by a
      misbehaving gateway, or the preimage as its recovery artifact.
- [ ] The runbook entry says "not proven lost, not proven recoverable", gives the duplicated-client
      check as the FIRST diagnostic framed as cheapest-to-rule-out, and does not claim the seed
      alone enables a second claimant.
- [ ] The forfeit path is documented as NORMALLY `Refunded`, with the claim/refund race
      (`lnv2-client/lib.rs:705-725`) that can promote it to send-`Success` named explicitly. An
      assertion that forfeit can never strand FAILS this criterion.
- [ ] The daily stranded check still fires: the ledger anchor substring is either unchanged or the
      runbook grep was updated in the same change, and a test pins whichever was chosen.
- [ ] No test asserts a receive-failure string that cannot occur; `"forfeited"` appears in no
      assertion.
- [ ] `cargo test` passes inside `nix develop` and behaviour is unchanged: no state-machine edit,
      no new money path.

Ledger anchor preserved and pinned by stranded_outcome_keeps_the_runbook_anchor; runbook is now the canonical operator account. Gate green (fmt/clippy/test) inside nix develop. Merged as ab3ad9c.

title: wallet-web: on-screen polling, degraded-daemon banner, /healthz
description:
`wallet-web`: on-screen polling, degraded-daemon banner, /healthz.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.4, §6c.6. Depends on the read surface.

Required:
1. ~50 lines of VANILLA JS compiled into the binary, doing two jobs only: polling on-screen
   operations, and disabling a submit button after click. No framework, no htmx, no bundler, no npm,
   no CDN. (Note: the button disable is a convenience — the real double-submit defence is
   render-time idempotency keys + PRG in br-t8f, because the UI must work without JS.)
2. Polling: GET /v1/operations/{key} every 3s for VISIBLE operations, stopping on terminal status
   and on `visibilitychange`. Polling is a live-view convenience, NOT the tracking mechanism —
   Outstanding is. Browsers throttle background timers and suspend mobile pages.
3. **Polling requests must be PASSIVE with respect to the session**: they must not slide
   `last_seen`, or an open tab stays authorized for the full 24h and the idle timeout never fires.
   (Enforced in br-nfz; do not defeat it here by routing polling through an activity-updating path.)
4. UI degrades honestly without JS: forms work, pages just do not live-update.
5. Daemon unreachable: READ PAGES render a clear banner. (The money/admin form-disable behaviour is
   specified in the plan but is NOT verified here: those forms are built by br-t8f and br-ucq, which
   this task does not depend on, so asserting them here would be impossible in the declared order.
   That integration check belongs to the final gate, br-4yz.)
6a. NOTE the asymmetry: a DOWN sidecar cannot answer at all, so sidecar-down is signalled to the
   supervisor by CONNECTION FAILURE, not by a field. /healthz answers only for a LIVE sidecar and
   reports {sidecar_alive: true, daemon_reachable: <bool>}. Do not claim the endpoint distinguishes
   both states by payload; it cannot.
6. `GET /healthz` is an explicit, deliberate exception to "every route requires a session" — a
   supervisor cannot log in. Restrict it to exactly two booleans (sidecar alive, daemon reachable).
   It MUST expose no balance, no operation, no federation, and no version detail, and it must be in
   the route-manifest allowlist so the carve-out is asserted rather than accidental.

Tests: polling stops at terminal status; continuous polling does not extend a session (covered in
br-nfz item 5 — do not regress it); degraded banner appears on read pages; /healthz
reports {sidecar_alive: true, daemon_reachable: <bool>} and leaks nothing else (sidecar-down is a
CONNECTION FAILURE, not a payload -- see item 6a).

Scope guard: no SSE, no WebSockets, no service worker, no notifications (ADR-0028 deferred all).
No second JS file, no build step.
7. OWN THE SHARED DEGRADED-STATE CONTRACT. Expose one reachability signal plus the form-marker
   convention (e.g. a template helper / CSS marker) that br-t8f and br-ucq apply to their own
   forms. Those beads render the disabled state; this bead defines the mechanism they call, so the
   behaviour has ONE implementation owner rather than being discovered missing at the final gate.
8. Define the SUBMIT-DISABLE contract too (the JS's second job): a documented form marker that
   br-t8f and br-ucq apply. This bead defines and unit-tests the mechanism; br-4yz verifies it
   against the real money and admin forms once they exist.

Copy canon (roadmap-to-v1.md 6b notes) applies to every user-facing string this bead renders --
including login, settings and error text: never "risk engine", "safe", "bank", "mint" as a verb,
"curated", or "anonymous".
The degraded-mode text is the sharpest case: it must say plainly that the wallet daemon is not
responding, not reassure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Polling updates a visible operation and stops on terminal status and on visibilitychange.
- [ ] Polling does NOT extend the session idle timer (the assertion lives in br-nfz; this bead must not defeat it by routing polling through an activity-updating path).
- [ ] Read pages render a clear banner when the daemon is unreachable. The money/admin form-disable check belongs to br-4yz, where those forms exist.
- [ ] /healthz distinguishes sidecar-alive from daemon-reachable and exposes NOTHING else: no balance, no operation, no federation, no version.
- [ ] The UI still functions with JavaScript disabled: forms submit, pages simply do not live-update.
- [ ] Total JavaScript stays under roughly 50 lines, with no framework, bundler, or npm dependency.
- [ ] The degraded-state contract is documented and callable by other surfaces, not private to
      this bead's read pages.
- [ ] The submit-disable marker is documented and exercised, not merely asserted to exist.
- [ ] The degraded-mode and health strings conform to the copy canon and state the real condition.
- [ ] The ACTUAL polling endpoint, hit continuously with a valid session, does not slide
      `last_seen`; likewise /healthz presented with a cookie. br-nfz can only test a synthetic
      passive route because the real one does not exist at its stage, so if this bead routes polling
      through an activity-updating path BOTH beads pass while the idle timeout is defeated.

title: Bound the preview under join_lock; recovery terminal-visibility window
description:
## Outcome
Two money-safe concurrency/visibility refinements on the recovery path, surfaced by the
multi-reviewer-loop over the merged br-m9m PR (#11). Neither is a money-safety defect.

## 1. Unbounded preview under join_lock (join family)
MultiClient::recover (multi_client.rs:305-316) holds join_lock across an UNBOUNDED
ClientBuilder::preview — an unreachable/slow fed makes recover hold join_lock indefinitely,
queueing all future joins/recoveries (NOT money ops — pay/receive/move don't take join_lock).
This is PRE-EXISTING: user-initiated join() (join_inner with deadline=None) has the same pattern;
only the scheduler's join_before_deadline bounds the preview. The comment at multi_client.rs:302-304
falsely says "bounded preview fetch". Fix: bound the preview fetch under a deadline for the join
FAMILY (join + recover), and correct the comment. Re-verify recover's reservation invariants hold
when preview times out (Drop drops the reservation; fresh partition never allocated → safe).

## 2. Recovery terminal-visibility window
Between complete_recovery's commit and the in-memory clients.insert (multi_client.rs:379-382), a
status GET observes the intent as succeeded while /v1/balance can still read 0 for the fed. Narrow
(microsecond window), money-safe, self-correcting on the next poll. Fix: gate terminal status/balance
reads on active_recoveries so the op reads in-progress until the client is installed.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Preview fetch under join_lock is bounded for join + recover; comment corrected.
- [ ] A status/balance read during the commit->insert window does not report succeeded+zero-balance.
- [ ] cargo fmt/clippy/test green (nix develop); recovery reservation invariants re-verified.
close_reason: Merged in PR #16: bounded the preview under join_lock (recover + join, 60s cap) and closed the recovery commit->insert visibility window (is_recovering-gated status). Gate green (706 tests); codex adversarial pass clean; reservation invariants re-verified.

A concurrent watch-cycle write to the same candidate key can conflict-fail an hours-long recovery replay's commit. Outcome is SAFE (partition never registered, intent Failed, retry recovers into a fresh prefix) but wasteful — a whole replay discarded on a commit conflict. Add autocommit-retry to the complete_recovery commit. Not a money-safety defect; efficiency/robustness only.

title: Live devimint recovery gate — pre-deploy blocker for seed recovery
description:
## Outcome
The seed-recovery feature (br-m9m, landed) passes a live devimint recovery gate. **This MUST
pass before the pilot receives real funds** — it is the spec's mandatory acceptance
(`docs/wallet-recovery-spec.md` "Verification"), and it has never run.

## Why this exists
br-m9m recovery is verified in code (2 rb-lite convergences + 2 adversarial review rounds; an
auto-double-pay found, fixed, and re-confirmed closed), but has ZERO live validation. Recovery
is money-critical (rebuilds ecash from the seed), so a live end-to-end pass is required before
any real-funds deployment. Merged (PR #11) on code-verification strength with this gate as the
deploy blocker.

## The gate
Build devimint + the wallet binaries (see docs/devimint-runbook.md: `nix develop -c cargo build
--workspace --bins`, `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR=~/p/fedimint/target-nix`, `add_target_dir_to_path`;
1 fed suffices — `devimint --num-feds 1 dev-fed`). Then:
1. Join a fed, receive ecash (lnv2 — mind the await-send-before-await-receive ordering, release
   bins, gateway pw; see [[devimint-lnv2-reliable-validation]]).
2. Record the balance, seed, and invite.
3. Simulate total store loss: a FRESH data dir (empty client.db + empty journal.db), same seed —
   this is the UNregistered path recovery supports (D3 refuse-if-registered).
4. `walletd restore-mnemonic < seed.txt`, then `wallet-cli recover <invite>`, then `await-move`.
5. Assert the balance is restored after recovery completes.

## Traps (from memory)
Rebuild wallet-cli/walletd with the explicit CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR before every smoke (stale
binary trap, [[devimint-dev-fed-is-single-fed]]). devimint is a built binary, not on PATH by
default.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Live 1-fed devimint: fund -> fresh store -> restore-mnemonic + recover -> balance restored.
- [ ] The recovered fed is spendable (UserApproved, allocator-eligible) — send from it post-recovery.
close_reason: PASSED live and landed via PR #12 (0e522fe). wallet-cli/tests/smoke_recover_devimint.sh: two-phase live devimint gate — Phase A (whole-store loss, daemon) + Phase B (journal-only loss, standalone, orphaned partition), both restoring EXACTLY the pre-loss balance (zero slack), recovered fed UserApproved, and spendable over lnv2. Independently verified on a fresh devimint --num-feds 1 run: restored EXACTLY 491646 msat, RECOVER_GATE_EXIT=0. Produced via supervised rb-lite (watched closely: no assertion-weakening, main.rs change comment-only, live pass confirmed independently). Recovery is now cleared for real-funds deploy.

title: Implement route_economics_by_pair (per-pair economic move floor)
description:
## Outcome
Implement `route_economics_by_pair`: a per-federation-ordered-pair economic move floor,
IO-supplied into the `AllocatorSnapshot` so `decide()` stays pure, that suppresses the
uneconomic-churn the flat/proportional caps cannot. Design is fully settled in
`docs/route-economics-decisions.md` (br-ljj.3) — implement it without reopening the design.

## Scope (per the five settled decisions + the adjacent finding)
1. Snapshot field `route_economics_by_pair[(from,to)] -> { resolved_gateway, min_viable_amount,
   status: Routable | Unroutable | UneconomicAtAnySize }`, populated by IO in `tick.rs`
   (today the snapshot is fee-thin: only `max_fee`, `max_fee_bps_of_move`, `min_move`).
2. Gateway selection: replace the Move path's FIRST-validating-gateway pick
   (executor.rs ~260-282) with the CHEAPEST gateway serving BOTH ends, computed from the same
   fee quotes the floor needs (argmin combined fed+gateway fee). `resolved_gateway` is that pick.
3. `min_viable_amount`: a fixed ~4-quote affine UPPER-bound model (round every fee component up)
   + a hard per-tick quote cap. No unbounded in-tick search. Over-blocking is the safe direction.
4. `gateway: Option<GatewayUrl>` (`#[serde(default)]`) on `Action::Move` and `Action::Evacuate`,
   stamped by `decide()` from `resolved_gateway`. `assemble_record` (executor.rs ~199-232) uses
   it as the cached gateway; the field enters the persisted Intent format (hence serde default).
5. Perform-time fallback (Q2): use `action.gateway` iff it still validates (serves both ends);
   else re-resolve (cheapest serving both ends) under the UNCHANGED proportional `fee_cap` — the
   cap, not gateway identity, is the money backstop. Record the actual gateway in
   `OperationKind::Move.gateway`.
6. `pinned_gateway` precedence (Q4): the pin overrides route economics entirely; compute the
   pair against the pin; `UneconomicAtAnySize` under a pin is still surfaced.
7. Fallbacks (Q5): missing entry -> permissive protocol floor (`min_move`); `Routable` ->
   `min_viable_amount`; `Unroutable` -> skip the pair's funding; `UneconomicAtAnySize` -> skip
   AND surface VISIBLY (a persistent diagnostic / refusal reason — it silently disables
   rebalancing for the pair forever otherwise).

## Non-goals
Does not change the proportional-cap knob. Does not add caching of route economics (stale-low is
the unsafe direction — computed fresh every tick, ~4 quotes/pair × 2 pairs).

## Critical constraints
`UneconomicAtAnySize` MUST be visible (unlike the deliberately-silent sub-dust skip). Any floor
approximation MUST be an explicit UPPER bound (under-estimating churns forever; over-blocking
self-heals). Money-adjacent allocator code: implement carefully with dual-review.

## Verification
- Golden tests: each status branch (Routable/Unroutable/UneconomicAtAnySize + missing-entry
  permissive fallback); the upper-bound floor's monotonicity; the cheapest-both-ends selection;
  the perform-time hint-with-cap fallback.
- Live devimint: a pair whose bps is below the combined ppm defers (UneconomicAtAnySize,
  surfaced); a viable pair moves; the move takes the cheaper of two serving gateways.
- `cargo test && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check` (run inside `nix develop`).

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Evacuate: fall back to a two-gateway Lightning hop when no gateway serves both feds
description:
Give `Evacuate` a second route: a real Lightning hop when no gateway serves both federations.

Authority: [ADR-0029](docs/adr/0029-evacuation-must-be-executable.md).
DEPENDS ON br-remove-gateway-pin-yjw for TWO distinct things, only one of which is the pin:
(1) its required change 1 supplies the per-guardian gateway REGISTRATION this bead's live gate
needs -- devimint's empty vetted list, not the pin, is what blocks that gate, and registration
alone unblocks it; (2) ADR-0030 makes automated routing unpinnable, which is what lets this bead
DELETE its four-case pin table rather than specify it on a money path.
ALSO DEPENDS ON br-y2j for INTERFACE SEQUENCING: both change how an evacuation's cap is computed
and persisted, and br-y2j establishes that shape first. Note the earlier rationale was wrong in BOTH directions: the absolute cap does not categorically
chunk-drain a hop evacuation either. Per ADR-0029 the outcome depends on the gateway's fee SHAPE
-- a summed two-leg quote within the cap chunk-drains; one strictly
above it at EVERY amount (not merely at the desired size, which downsizes) refuses in a retryable
livelock, because `total_within_cap` compares
`receive_quote + send_quote <= fee_cap` (`fee.rs:163`) -- equality executes. Two gateway bases totalling 150
sats against the old 50-sat cap leave no candidate that fits. Do not write a pre-change test that
assumes chunk-drain.

## The problem

Every cross-federation transfer resolves ONE gateway that serves both ends.
`resolve_move_gateway` and `resolve_fallback_move_gateway` both return a single `GatewayUrl` gated
on `gateway_serves_route(to, from)`; the so-called fallback resolver only searches for a CHEAPER
gateway that still serves both. NOTE the correct shape: `MovePlan` is explicitly GATEWAY-FREE (move_protocol.rs:85-102). The
single gateway lives in `MoveParams` and the durable `MoveRecord` (move_protocol.rs:68-82,
wallet-core/src/types.rs:482-501 (NOTE: wallet-core, not the 9-line wallet-fedimint re-export shim)), is copied into a one-gateway ledger field (ledger.rs:127-135,
journal.rs:2984-3002), and is reused on replay (executor.rs:234-274, 1942-1951). A global pin
currently wins unconditionally (executor.rs:277-305).
`move_protocol.rs` states it explicitly: "LN-only: v1 validates that the destination-selected
gateway also serves the source, giving the same internal-swap route as `Move`. No peg-out."

For `Move` that is fine -- routine rebalancing can decline and wait. For `Evacuate` it means a
dying federation with no shared gateway CANNOT be drained, which is the one case where refusing
costs money.

The primitives already exist and were exercised by hand: during the 2026-07-28 canary the wallet
paid an invoice minted by a DIFFERENT federation's gateway over real Lightning (walletd via
ostracoda paying an Afribit Kibera invoice via the Fedi/Henwen gateways). Only the move path
PERSISTS a single committed route -- not a "pin"; a pin is the standing selection override
ADR-0030 removes, whereas a persisted route is replayed as recorded.

## Required changes

1. `Evacuate` only. Do NOT extend `Move`: it keeps the swap-only path and its cheaper fee
   (measured: internal send leg 8,948 vs external 16,064 msat on 1,000,000).
2. STRICT ordering, and it stays strict even when it costs operations. Always attempt the
   shared-gateway swap first, because it is cheaper. Reach the Lightning hop ONLY when no gateway
   SERVES both ends. The hop must never pre-empt a swap that serves -- with ONE bounded exception, which ADR-0029 states and which covers
   BOTH truncation causes: the candidate-COUNT bound (an oversized list) AND the WALL-TIME bound
   (a short, honest list whose gateways answer slowly can exhaust the per-class deadline). Either
   way the hop may be reached without every shared candidate having been examined -- an honest
   list is not guaranteed a complete scan, only a bounded one. Read
   "never" as "never among the candidates examined"; stated unconditionally it would require
   waiting out an adversarially grown list and strand the funds.
   DECIDED, because the two goals in ADR-0029 can now disagree: if a shared route serves only a
   small net (a high-ppm gateway has a narrow feasible window under the base+proportional cap)
   while a hop pair would serve the full drain, THE SWAP STILL WINS and the source drains in
   several operations. Chunking is slow rather than lossy ONLY BECAUSE 2b's economic-viability check forces every chunk
   to deliver at least what it costs; without that condition this ruling burns the balance (see
   ADR-0029's Amendment). Do not quote the unconditional form. The alternative to the ruling is
   sizing both route classes on every tick to compare them -- do not add that comparison.
2b. DEFINE "serves" precisely -- registry presence is NOT the test, and this is the operational
   definition [ADR-0029 carries](docs/adr/0029-evacuation-must-be-executable.md) in its Amendment
   section:
     A gateway SERVES a shared route when it is on BOTH federations' vetted lists, VALIDATES,
     and the br-y2j affordability search over THAT route returns an affordable
   amount AND that amount passes the b-bis ECONOMIC VIABILITY post-check (`total_fee <= n*`).
   Both terms are required: viability is a post-check on the search result, not part of the
   search, so a route whose `n*` fails it satisfies the affordability half yet does NOT serve
   per ADR-0029's Amendment and CONTEXT.md's **Serves** entry. A hop LEG
     is served by a gateway on the ONE federation's list at that end, each leg judged separately.
   THIS BEAD OWNS CLOSING THE BOTH-LISTS GAP, because nothing else does and ADR-0030 rule 1 is
   false in the code until it is closed. Today shared candidates are enumerated from the
   DESTINATION's list alone (`executor.rs:344`, `route_econ.rs:304`) and the source end is checked
   only by fetching `routing_info`, so a gateway vetted solely by the destination can carry an
   automated move -- routing money outside the source federation's vetted list.
   REQUIRED: enumerate shared candidates from the INTERSECTION of the two vetted lists.
   AND FOR `Evacuate`, A HOLDING HINT DOES NOT SHORT-CIRCUIT SELECTION -- CONTEXT.md's Route hint
   entry and the archive banner both assign this rule to this bead, so it is stated here: for
   `Move` a hint that still holds is kept ONLY AFTER being priced against the cap (holding is
   membership+validation, so a hint can hold while its fee has risen above the cap -- catch that
   here, not at the receive step which is permanent or the pay step which retries the persisted
   route), but an `Evacuate` hint is only a starting point, and
   the route class is selected by LARGEST SIZED EXECUTED NET (2c). Honouring a holding hint that
   sizes to a small viable chunk while another candidate drains far more re-creates the
   repeated-operation cumulative-base-fee failure ADR-0029 exists to fix.
   AND RE-CHECK MEMBERSHIP ON THE HINT PATH (`executor.rs:306-319`), which fresh enumeration does
   NOT cover: a hint priced before the source federation revoked that gateway is accepted today on
   endpoint validation alone, so money routes outside the source's vetted list without any fresh
   enumeration ever running. CONTEXT.md's Route hint entry names this bead as what closes it, and
   the pin bead's scope guard must not be read as freezing it. Add an AC for a SOURCE-REVOKED
   HINT: an action carrying a gateway since removed from the source's list must be re-resolved,
   not honoured. Without this the caveats get dropped (below) while the hazard remains open.
   THIS APPLIES TO `Move` TOO, and "Do NOT extend this to `Move`" must not be read as excluding
   it. That scope guard is about the ROUTE SHAPE and the cap -- `Move` keeps the swap-only path
   and its proportional cap -- not about which vetted lists a shared candidate must be on. If
   `Move` keeps enumerating from the destination's list alone it keeps routing money through
   gateways the source federation never vetted, which ADR-0030 rule 1 forbids for ALL automated
   routing, not just evacuation. Add a `Move` test that rejects a destination-only gateway.
   ADR-0029's Amendment and CONTEXT.md currently mark the both-lists half as "intent, not today's
   behaviour" and say not to cite it as holding; when this bead lands, BOTH must drop that caveat
   -- it is this bead that makes the invariant true.
   Being unable to fund the FULL ask is NOT a failure to serve: `InsufficientBalanceError` at the
   desired amount is the documented DOWNSIZE signal (`executor.rs:862-872`), never a fall-through
   trigger. Reading it as one would route every full-balance evacuation onto the ~80% dearer hop
   while a healthy shared gateway sat idle.
   This has a structural consequence the bead must state: route selection can no longer run BEFORE
   sizing (today it does, `executor.rs:1301-1302`). Each candidate route is sized with ITS OWN
   receive/send fee bases under br-y2j's search, and only the resulting executed net is compared
   with that route's derived cap. Specify where route selection sits relative to
   `size_fresh_evacuation` in the new flow; a quote-first implementation rejects every
   full-balance route before sizing and refuses evacuations that are perfectly affordable. A shared
   gateway that is registered but dead or unpriceable must FALL THROUGH to the hop, or the
   evacuation livelocks in exactly the incident the hatch exists for. THIS BEAD DECIDES THE
   PREDICATE; do not leave it to the implementer:
     - A shared-gateway swap is UNAVAILABLE FOR THIS ATTEMPT when it is absent from EITHER
       federation's vetted list, validation fails, its fee quotes error, they do not return within
       the existing per-quote timeout, it QUOTES BUT DOES NOT PERFORM (a bounded record of recent
       perform-level `receive`/`pay` failures per gateway -- CONTEXT.md's **Serves** carries the
       same term, and without it a request-level misbehaving gateway is reselected every tick),
       or br-y2j's affordability search OVER THAT ROUTE returns
       `Ok(None)` AND that `None` is an ANALYTICALLY PROVEN structural refusal (2c(c)) -- an
       INCONCLUSIVE `None` is RETRYABLE and must NOT mark the swap unavailable nor license the
       dearer hop: the bounded
   search found no amount under its derived cap, which is
   NOT proof that none exists: br-y2j owns that search and ADR-0029 accepts its incompleteness, so
   a feasible window beyond the probed boundaries reads as `Ok(None)` too. Distinguish an
   ANALYTICALLY PROVEN structural refusal (2c(c)'s two conditions) from an inconclusive bounded
   miss; treating the latter as the former falls through to the dearer hop with a viable shared
   route still available, or its best fitting amount FAILS THE ECONOMIC
       VIABILITY CHECK in br-y2j's economic-viability check (2c b-bis) (`total_fee > n*`). Membership is CHECKED, not assumed: a
       candidate that validates both ends but is vetted by only one federation is UNAVAILABLE.
       THE HOP GETS THE SAME CHECK, and needs it more: it stacks two gateways' bases and is ~80%
       dearer on the send leg, so its floor efficiency is worse than a shared route's. Falling
       through to a hop that also only carries uneconomic chunks burns the balance at a HIGHER
       rate. If neither class has an economically viable candidate, stay `Retryable` -- strand
       rather than burn, per ADR-0018.
       NOT unavailability: a single over-cap quote at any ONE amount, and never
       `InsufficientBalanceError` at the full ask. Both are downsize signals
       (`executor.rs:862-872`). Judging a route by one quote at the desired amount is the
       quote-first mistake requirement 2b exists to forbid: it falls every full-balance
       evacuation through to the ~80% dearer hop while a serving gateway sits idle.
     - On unavailable, the hop is attempted AS SOON AS COVERAGE COMPLETES -- not after N
       further ticks of backoff. When the shared list fits in one scan window (the common case, and the
       case the AC below fixtures) every candidate is examined in the FIRST tick, so this is
       same-tick. When it does not, "one failed quote is enough" applies per CANDIDATE, not per
       LIST: a dead candidate is retired from the sweep immediately rather than retried, but the
       hop is still reached only after this tick's scan window is exhausted (2c). Do not
       read this bullet as licensing a hop while examined shared candidates remain -- that is the strict-ordering violation
       2c exists to prevent. waiting K ticks on a dying federation is the cost the evacuation lead
       cannot absorb. TWO DIFFERENT LEADS EXIST -- do not conflate them. The one this argument
       rests on is the DETECTION lead, `SHUTDOWN_EVACUATION_LEAD_SECS = 86_400`
       (`wallet-fedimint/src/probe.rs:202`): how long before `federation_expiry_timestamp` the
       wallet starts treating a federation as shutting down, i.e. the whole window in which
       retries can happen. The other is `WatchPolicy::evacuation_lead_ms`, default ONE HOUR
       (`wallet-core/src/watch.rs:56`), which is only the scheduler's wake granularity near
       expiry (`watch.rs:176-186`). ADR-0018 is cited by the 24h constant's doc comment for the
       leave-before-expiry PRINCIPLE, but ADR-0018 states no number -- do not cite it for one.
     - The NEXT tick re-tries swap-first from scratch -- but ONLY while backfill proves that
       NEITHER a receive nor a send operation has committed. Once either artifact exists the
       PERSISTED ROUTE IS AUTHORITATIVE through settlement, and no re-resolution may occur.
       Without that boundary, "re-try swap-first" and requirement 5's "no re-resolution"
       contradict each other: after a hop receive commits, re-running swap-first would either
       mint a second invoice or change the source gateway under an invoice already sized and
       recorded for the original hop, leaving fees, persisted route and ledger disagreeing.
       Pre-commit candidate exhaustion remains `Retryable`.
   This is deliberately biased toward falling through: the hop costs ~80% more on the send leg
   (16,064 vs 8,948 msat per 1,000,000), and paying that occasionally beats stranding a balance.
2c. ROUTE SELECTION when several pairs exist. Scan shared candidates first, then source/destination
   hop pairs, and CONTINUE PAST a pair whose quote fails or exceeds the
   cap rather than refusing on the first one -- today failed quotes are skipped but plain
   validation can re-select the same unpriceable gateway (`executor.rs:404-416`, `:441-455`).
   Within each route class pick the candidate with the LARGEST SIZED EXECUTED NET; break ties on
   lower total fee, then on CANDIDATE IDENTITY lexicographically -- the gateway URL for a shared
   candidate, the ordered pair `(source_url, destination_url)` for a hop. "On gateway URL" is
   under-defined for a hop and lets two conforming implementations persist different pairs from
   identical registry state, the divergence this requirement exists to forbid. Stability across runs is NOT a property this design provides: the SDK
   re-permutes the list per call, so which candidates a truncated scan examines varies. That is
   accepted -- every examined candidate has passed the cap and the viability check, so the choice
   among them is an efficiency question, not a safety one. Do not restate it as an ordering guarantee.
   BOUND THE SCAN. The pair space is |source list| x |destination list|, and each surviving pair
   costs TWO `routing_info` LEGS -- but FETCH PER UNIQUE
   `(federation, gateway)` LEG, ONCE FOR THE WHOLE PERFORM, and reuse it across every pair that
   mentions that leg AND across both sizing passes. Per-PAIR fetching repeats identical lookups:
   two six-gateway lists need 12 unique leg snapshots but would make up to 72 calls, and at the
   10-second request timeout that alone can exhaust `perform_timeout`. Re-fetching between passes lets a gateway fee change move the slope after pass 1 fixed
   its bound, so pass 2 can miss a feasible amount or return `Retryable`, and it doubles the
   latency the wall-time bound is trying to contain. Only the LOCAL dry-run quotes are per pass;
   two network fetches is the worst case per candidate (one per leg;
   a hop necessarily has distinct source and destination gateways and both legs are repriced) -- 
   plus a sizing search of LOCAL fee quotes (br-y2j owns that budget and states it PER PASS:
   worst case past 100, not the stale ~50 single-bisection figure). The
   local quotes are cheap (`Client::fee_quote` is a DB transaction, no network) -- the bound that
   matters is the NETWORK one, and the reason it needs a hard limit rather than a soft one is
   ADR-0030's union finding: a single guardian can inject arbitrary entries into a vetted list,
   so neither list's length is trusted input.
   BOUND THE SCAN, SIMPLY. The candidate space is |shared list| for the swap and
   `{(s, d) : s in source, d in destination, s != d}` for the hop -- EXCLUDE THE DIAGONAL, since
   where the lists overlap the raw product contains `(g, g)`, which is not a hop (CONTEXT.md: a
   hop is TWO gateways) and pricing it with external-send assumptions would persist an unavailable
   shared gateway as one. Scan at most N candidates per route class per tick, in the order `gateways()`
   returns -- which already fronts the most widely vetted --
   and select the largest sized executed net among those examined. Do NOT build a cross-tick
   sweep: no persisted examined-set, no sweep generations, no cross-tick coverage
   deadline, no detection timestamp. (That strikes the DURABLE sweep's deadline machinery -- it
   does NOT strike the per-tick wall-time cap required below, which is a bound on one tick's work,
   not a cross-tick budget.) Journal it when a list exceeds N and the scan was truncated.
   SIZE N PER CLASS, AND SIZE THE HOP'S AGAINST THE PAIR SPACE. The shared class is one entry per
   gateway, so a small N (32) covers any honest list. THE HOP CLASS IS CARTESIAN --
   `|source| x |destination|` -- and two honest SIX-gateway lists already make 36 pairs, so a flat
   32 would exclude an ordinary, non-adversarial evacuation's only viable pair and strand it. The
   hop's bound is a FIXED CONSTANT chosen to cover the honest pair space -- never
   computed FROM the product, which is attacker-controlled since the union is unbounded. Two
   DISJOINT six-gateway lists give 36 pairs, so 36 is the floor if six-per-side is the design
   point.
   Traversing the product across ticks is NOT an alternative here: this design keeps no cross-tick
   state and takes a fresh prefix of an order the SDK reshuffles per call, so there is nothing to
   advance. ADR-0029 is the authority and states the same.
   WHAT THIS GIVES UP. An honest list fits in one window, so strict swap-first holds exactly as
   ADR-0029 requires. Beyond the honest sizing, the only way to exceed N is a guardian injecting
   entries -- and that guardian is already inside the federation
   the user trusts with custody, with cheaper ways to hurt them. The residual under that attack is
   that a serving swap can fall outside the window and the evacuation takes the ~80% dearer hop:
   an efficiency loss, still bounded by the fee cap and the viability post-check, and
   never a burn -- see the residual note below for why "never a stranding" is too strong. An earlier draft specified durable cross-process sweep state,
   per-class deadlines and a new persisted detection timestamp to convert that bounded
   inefficiency into an optimal route under active attack; that was mechanism no requirement
   here needed.
   BE HONEST ABOUT THE RESIDUAL, as ADR-0029 is. The window is SUPPORT-ORDERED -- `gateways()`
   shuffles then STABLE-sorts by peers-lacking -- so it is randomised only WITHIN ties, and this
   is not sampling. A low-support serving candidate behind a full window of higher-support entries
   is excluded DETERMINISTICALLY every tick, so "never a stranding" holds only while a viable hop
   is selected. Conversely a one-guardian injection sorts LAST and cannot displace a widely-vetted
   candidate. The accepted price of carrying no cross-tick state is that a persistently
   out-of-window serving swap is never reached; the hop is what covers it.
   BOUND THE SCAN BY WALL TIME TOO, not only by candidate count: two `routing_info` round-trips per
   candidate against slow-but-responsive gateways can exhaust `perform_timeout` before the hop is
   reached, cancelling the operation and restarting the scan from nothing. Cap elapsed time per
   route class so the hop is always attempted inside the operation's budget AND SETTLEMENT STILL
   FITS. A budget sized only to REACH the hop can consume `perform_timeout` before invoice creation
   and payment, cancelling the future so the next tick restarts the scan -- a livelock that
   satisfies "the hop was attempted" while never completing.
   AC: with shared candidates that respond slowly and all fail viability, the evacuation
   COMPLETES over the hop within one `perform` budget -- assert completion, not merely that the
   hop was reached.
   AC: with overlapping source and destination vetted lists, no `(g, g)` pair is priced or
   persisted as a hop.
   NEITHER a fixed prefix NOR a positional cursor is sound as the traversal primitive: `gateways()`
   shuffles then stable-sorts by peers-lacking (`fedimint-lnv2-client/src/api.rs:96-113`), so the
   list is re-permuted per call. Take the first N of each call's ordering; do not index into it.
   Record how many candidates were examined and whether the scan was truncated, so a truncated
   scan is visible rather than looking like an empty candidate list.
   AC: with a shared list LONGER THAN THE SCAN BOUND (N = 32) in which exactly ONE named gateway
   serves, the evacuation
   is selected when the scan reaches it, and the hop is not taken while it is examined and
   serving. State the AC in IDENTITIES, never positions -- "the K+1'th candidate" is not well defined when the SDK
   re-permutes. The test MUST re-permute the returned order between ticks; that is the case a
   positional cursor silently fails.
   AC: with a shared list longer than the scan bound, the evacuation still completes -- taking
   the hop if no examined candidate serves -- rather than stalling.
   Deliberately NOT specified: a quote budget, an adaptive/priority scheduler, or per-pair
   timeouts. The bounded per-tick scan above covers the hazard; the rest is mechanism no requirement here needs. (An
   earlier draft closed with "the constant cap plus the SDK's existing sort covers the hazard".
   That sentence endorsed the two designs recorded as FAILED at the top of this requirement and
   is struck; it is not an alternative an implementer may take.)
   Do NOT copy today's cheapest-fitting rule (`executor.rs:390`, `:436`) unexamined: it compares
   candidates at a COMMON `plan.amount` (`executor.rs:419`), which no longer exists once serves
   requires per-candidate sizing -- "cheapest" would then compare fees charged at DIFFERENT
   amounts. Concretely: gateway X serves 1,000 sats for 60 sats, gateway Y serves 72,000 sats for
   1,500 sats. Cheapest picks X -- ~72 operations and ~4,300 sats of cumulative base fees against
   one 1,500-sat operation through Y -- inverting ADR-0029's one-operation goal on identical
   registry state. Without a stated objective,
   identical registry state can persist different gateway pairs and spend materially different
   real fees while both implementations claim compliance.
   Refuse only when every candidate EXAMINED THIS TICK has failed, and say so in the diagnostic
   -- including whether the scan was truncated. Without
   this, a 250-sat-base destination gateway refuses a 1,000-sat evacuation under the 230-sat cap
   even though another offered gateway would fit.
3. The two-gateway shape: mint the invoice on the destination through a gateway that serves the
   DESTINATION, and pay it from the source through a gateway that serves the SOURCE. These are
   different gateways; the plan currently cannot express that.
4. No bar on the destination gateway -- take whichever the destination federation offers. During
   an evacuation a worse counterparty beats stranding the balance, and every additional gate is
   another way the escape hatch fails to open. Both legs stay hash-locked, so this adds no new
   trust (see ADR-0029 Consequences).
4b. RE-PRICE BOTH LEGS. Fresh evacuation sizing currently hardwires ONE gateway and the
   internal-swap `send_fee_minimum` discount (executor.rs:744, :805), which does not apply across
   two gateways, while the eventual pay recheck uses the invoice-aware source-gateway fee
   (executor.rs:1455, multi_client.rs:916). Pre-sizing must use the destination's receive fee plus
   the SOURCE gateway's EXTERNAL-send fee, or the hop is sized against a discount it will not get.

5. PERSIST THE ROUTE DURABLY and define replay. The record currently holds ONE gateway; a hop
   needs both identities, a route kind, and operator-visible recording in the ledger.
   NO PIN PRECEDENCE IS NEEDED: per [ADR-0030](docs/adr/0030-automated-routing-is-never-pinned.md)

   scheduler-, allocator- and probe-driven paths this bead governs always resolve from the vetted
   list. The surviving standalone `--gateway` break-glass is operator-invoked and touches no
   automated decision, so it raises no route-selection question here. An earlier draft of this
   bead specified a four-case pin table; it is deleted, not answered.
   Specify crash recovery at BOTH non-idempotent boundaries
   (cache-loss resume, and a crash after the receive but before the send), or a restart can route
   or pay differently than the first attempt while "one operation" still passes. The AC must
   therefore assert MORE than "exactly one operation" -- which is in any case WRONG at the SDK level:
   a hop is ONE wallet **Operation** driven by ONE **Intent** (not synonyms:
   the Operation is the glossary's user-facing unit, where the
   idempotency guarantee lives) containing TWO SDK operations, a receive and a send. Assert BOTH
   levels. Assert: exactly one receive op, exactly one send op, one invoice /
   payment hash, the exact persisted gateway identities and route kind, and NO re-resolution of
   the route -- at BOTH real POST-COMMIT killpoints with complete `MoveRecord` cache loss. Use the
   killpoints that already exist, NOT the pre-commit lines an earlier draft cited:
   `before-move-record` (`executor.rs:1398` -- receive op committed in the client DB, `MoveRecord`
   not yet persisted) and `after-send-commit` (`executor.rs:1517` -- send op committed,
   `MoveRecord` does not yet carry `send_op`). A test at the old :1353/:1500 lines can pass
   without ever exercising a committed receive or send. Note op-log backfill currently DISCARDS each
   SDK operation's gateway (`multi_client.rs:1226-1259`; `SendOperationMeta.gateway` does exist at
   our pinned rev, `fedimint-lnv2-client/src/lib.rs:90`), so backfill must be extended too.

   leave it to be found: extending `OpArtifact` recovers each EXISTING op's own gateway, and at
   `before-move-record` only the RECEIVE op exists. The source gateway and the shared-vs-hop kind
   are in no committed artifact there, so replay would have to RE-RESOLVE them -- which that AC
   and the commit boundary in 2b both forbid.

   and BOTH gateway identities into the receive operation's `MoveMeta`, alongside the clamped
   amount and the final cap, with `#[serde(default)]` on the new fields so pre-change rows still

   others undecodable on upgrade. A route kind and a second gateway also change the durable
   `MoveRecord` (journal `TAG_MOVE`, `journal.rs:66`) and the ledger's `OperationKind::Move`,

   optional/defaulted fields, and every one needs the SAME absent-case rule: a legacy row carrying

   was -- EXCEPT a receive-only row (`from=None`, `send_required=false`), i.e. a legacy
   `DirectInflow`, which shares this type, has no route to reconstruct, and must decode as
   receive-only rather than as a shared route through the existing gateway. Add old-row fixtures for each. "Greenfield: no compatibility shims" in the scope guard
   means no shims for behaviour; it has never meant breaking live persisted rows, and this bead
   must not be read that way.
   Reassembly prefers the `MoveMeta` route over any re-resolution. Do NOT re-open this at
   implementation time; it is the same decided class as the cap.
6. UPDATE THE DOCS THAT THIS CHANGE FALSIFIES: `docs/fedimint-mechanics.md` §5 (the "There is NO
   fallback when no shared gateway exists" passage), `docs/roadmap-to-v1.md` (the one-gateway
   invariant bullet), and -- the one that matters during an incident --
   `docs/real-sats-pilot-runbook.md:290-295`, which currently tells the operator that every move
   and every evacuation needs one gateway serving both federations, that a second gateway is a
   deliberate non-goal so there is no alternate route, and not to expect evacuation to rescue a
   gateway outage. That is the document they will be reading during exactly the incident this
   bead exists for. It must state that the hop exists for `Evacuate` only, when it triggers, that
   it costs more, and HOW TO VERIFY WHICH ROUTE WAS TAKEN from `history` / `show`. `docs/fedimint-mechanics.md` and `docs/roadmap-to-v1.md` have both been pre-corrected to say the
   hop is decided-but-not-built; when the code lands, those two must say it is built. The runbook
   entry has NOT been pre-corrected and must be written from scratch.
7. Preserve the existing two-leg guarantees on the new route: idempotent replay, the gross-up so
   the destination nets the intended amount, the §15.7 committed-contract check, and honest
   terminal classification. The hop changes WHICH gateways are used, not the settlement model.

## Tests

MANDATORY, because the bead's own requirement 2b is otherwise untested and the evacuation can
still livelock while every other criterion passes:
- A shared gateway that is REGISTERED but dead / timing out / unpriceable falls through to the
  hop. Note the current quote path skips failures and can fall back to plain validation that
  re-selects the same unpriceable gateway (executor.rs:404, :441), so this test must be written
  red-first against that behaviour.

- With no gateway serving both federations, an evacuation SUCCEEDS via the hop and the destination
  is credited the intended net amount. This case LIVELOCKS today (`resolve_gateway` returns
`ExecError::Retryable`, executor.rs:350-356, explicitly documented "Retryable, NOT Permanent ...
never terminally Failed" at :333-335) -- it is retried every tick forever, NOT refused. The
  pre-change assertion is therefore that the intent stays NON-TERMINAL (Retryable/Pending) across
  N ticks with no destination credit. Do NOT assert a terminal refusal: the code never produces
  one, so such a test either cannot go green pre-change or gets watered down into a vacuous one.
- With a shared gateway available, the swap is chosen and the hop is NOT attempted; assert on the
  route actually taken, not merely on success, or a hop-always implementation passes.
- The hop path is idempotent under replay: re-driving yields exactly ONE receive op, exactly ONE
  send op, one invoice / payment hash, the same persisted gateway identities and route kind, and
  no route re-resolution. Do NOT write "yields ONE operation" and stop there: it is ONE wallet
  Operation but TWO SDK operations, so the bare phrasing is either read as impossible or
  reinterpreted downward until it detects nothing. Assert one wallet Operation AND the two SDK
  ops explicitly.
-
- Live devimint gate: two federations with NO shared gateway, evacuation drains the source; exit
  codes captured, and one assertion deliberately broken first to prove the gate can fail.

## Gate prerequisites

The live gate needs TWO federations with DISJOINT gateway coverage. Per project experience
`dev-fed` starts ONE federation regardless of `--num-feds`, so two-fed runs need the existing
harness patch, PLUS new work to make a gateway serve only one federation. Budget these as part of
the bead; they are not incidental.

## Scope guard

Do NOT extend this to `Move`. Do NOT touch the per-federation balance cap -- ADR-0018 stands and
this route is best-effort, not a reliability guarantee, so nothing here justifies holding more per
federation. Do NOT add on-chain peg-out: ADR-0004 (lightning-only) holds and ADR-0018's
gateway-independent escape stays deferred. Do NOT add reputation, liquidity, or allowlist checks
on the destination gateway. Greenfield: no compatibility shims.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With no gateway serving both ends, an evacuation completes via a two-gateway Lightning hop
      and credits the intended net amount; the pre-change assertion must be that the intent stays non-terminal
      (Retryable/Pending) across N ticks -- NOT that it reaches a terminal Failed state, which
      never occurs.
- [ ] With a shared gateway that SERVES both ends, the swap route is taken and the hop is not
      attempted ("present" is not the test: a listed gateway that is dead or cannot price the
      route does not serve, and the body falls through to the hop in exactly that case) --
      asserted on the route, not on success alone.
- [ ] ROUTE RECOVERY (the requirement-5 criterion, stated in full because the short form was both
      weaker and wrong): at EACH of `before-move-record` (`executor.rs:1398`) and
      `after-send-commit` (`executor.rs:1517`), with the `MoveRecord` cache dropped entirely,
      replay yields exactly ONE receive op, exactly ONE send op, ONE invoice / payment hash, the
      SAME persisted gateway identities and route kind, and performs NO route re-resolution.
      "Exactly one operation" alone is not the criterion -- one WALLET operation, two SDK ops -- The failure it
      hides: op-log backfill discards the gateway (`OpArtifact` carries no gateway field,
      `multi_client.rs:1226-1259`), so after cache loss the send leg can execute through a
      DIFFERENT gateway than the one persisted and reported, on a path pre-sized with an
      internal-swap discount it will not get. (Do not justify this with "the pin wins
      unconditionally": true today, false on the daemon path once br-remove-gateway-pin-yjw --
      a blocking dependency -- lands. The backfill half sustains the AC on its own.)
- [ ] A hop evacuation is refused only when NO amount fits the cap, OR the best cap-fitting
      amount FAILS ECONOMIC VIABILITY *after* the `shortfall <= A` bounded probe below it has
      also failed (br-y2j mandates that probe; a top-only reading refuses at a note-count
      discontinuity where a smaller amount succeeds, then takes the dearer hop or strands)
      (`total_fee > n*` -- the route does not serve, per the body
      and ADR-0029's Amendment; this is a valid PRE-MINT refusal that an earlier revision of this
      criterion wrongly excluded, so a safe implementation would have VIOLATED the criterion while
      a conforming one could burn ~97% of the balance), OR the final pay-step re-quote fails EITHER the persisted cap OR the
      viability inequality (br-y2j requires re-checking both at Pay: the cap has a fixed base
      component, so a changed quote can sit under the cap while still costing more than it
      delivers) -- NOT when the first quote at the desired size is over
      cap, which must downsize instead. ADR-0029: "a single over-cap quote at the desired size is
      NOT a refusal". The terse form ("a hop over the fee cap is refused") blesses exactly the
      quote-first refusal requirement 2b forbids, and can strand an executable evacuation.
- [ ] `Move`'s ROUTE SHAPE and FEE-CAP behaviour are unchanged, asserted by test: it stays
      swap-only, never hops, and keeps its proportional cap. This is NOT a claim that `Move` is
      untouched -- requirement 2b deliberately changes which gateways it will accept.
- [ ] A `Move` whose candidate is on the DESTINATION's vetted list but not the SOURCE's is
      REJECTED, asserted by test.
- [ ] A `Move` carrying a route hint since REVOKED by the source federation is RE-RESOLVED, not
      honoured, asserted by test.
- [ ] The MIRRORED case: a hint since revoked by the DESTINATION federation is likewise
      re-resolved. Membership is a two-list predicate for a shared route and the hint path never
      re-enumerates, so a source-only implementation passes every other criterion while still
      honouring a hint the destination's guardians revoked.
- [ ] A live devimint gate drains a source federation with no shared gateway, is RUN not merely
      written, and is shown to go red when one assertion is deliberately broken.
- [ ] With a shared list of exactly ONE registered-but-dead/unpriceable gateway (fixture size pinned so it fits one scan window), it falls through to the hop IN THE SAME
      TICK,
      and the following tick re-tries swap-first -- but ONLY while backfill proves that NEITHER a
      receive nor a send operation has committed. Once either artifact exists the persisted route
      is authoritative and there is no re-try (body, requirement 5): re-routing after a commit
      can mint a second invoice or move the gateway beneath a committed route. Written red-first
      against today's re-selection behaviour (`executor.rs:404-416`, `:441-455`).
- [ ] The runbook's gateway-outage entry describes the hop, its `Evacuate`-only scope, its higher
      cost, and how to read the route actually taken.
