title: wallet-web: crate skeleton, config, init, fail-closed startup
description:
Create the `wallet-web` binary crate: config, `init`, fail-closed startup.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.0, §6c.1, §6c.6. Posture: ADR-0028.
The spec is authoritative and complete — follow it rather than improvising.

Required:
1. New workspace member `wallet-web` (binary). A CLIENT of walletd over HTTP with a bearer token,
   exactly like wallet-cli. NEVER opens client.db or journal.db (daemon holds exclusive locks).
2. Bind address is HARD-CODED to 127.0.0.1 — only the port is configurable (default 9737). Do not
   add a bind-address config option: it would let 0.0.0.0 satisfy this spec while breaking the
   fixed exposure posture.
3. The daemon URL must be http:// and its host an IP LITERAL in 127.0.0.0/8 or ::1. Reject DNS
   names outright -- including `localhost`, which resolves but is not a literal and can be
   repointed -- and reject non-http schemes. Fail startup otherwise, or a
   typo ships the full-access bearer token in plaintext to a remote host.
4. `wallet-web.toml`, written 0600 with the mode RE-ASSERTED after write (mirror
   wallet-daemon/src/config.rs). Holds: port, daemon URL, token path, Argon2id PHC hash, session
   idle/absolute timeouts, and `public_origin` (explicit scheme+host+port, NOT derived from Host).
5. `wallet-web init`: no-echo prompt, confirm, enforce a 12-char minimum, reject >1024-byte input
   BEFORE hashing, hash with Argon2id at pinned params (m=19456 KiB, t=2, p=1), write config.
6. Server REFUSES TO START with no hash, a malformed PHC string, or params below those minimums.
   Fail closed: no default credential, no "auth disabled until configured", no setup page.

Tests: init writes 0600; startup fails with no hash / malformed PHC / weak params; startup rejects
a non-loopback daemon URL (there is NO bind-address test -- the address is a hard-coded
constant, not configuration); passwords under 12 chars rejected;
oversized input rejected before hashing.

Scope guard: no routes, no auth logic, no templates here. Do NOT touch the daemon. No JS toolchain.
Greenfield: no backwards-compat or migration code.
7. Structured `tracing` logging is initialised at startup. The level comes from the RUST_LOG
   environment variable, NOT from wallet-web.toml -- the plan's config inventory is deliberately
   closed, and adding keys to it is out of scope. NEVER log the
   password, the session token, the daemon bearer token, or a full invoice -- at any level.
8. ADD `wallet-web` TO THE NIX BUILD. `flake.nix`'s `rustSrc` filters the source to an explicit
   list of the five existing crates; adding a workspace member without adding its directory there
   leaves `nix build` seeing a member that is not in the filtered source, and the build breaks.
   Add "wallet-web" to that `paths` list in the same change that adds the crate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] wallet-web builds as a workspace member and starts, serving nothing yet.
- [ ] The bind address is a hard-coded loopback constant: no config key can change it (the config struct has no bind-address field at all).
- [ ] Startup EXITS NON-ZERO with a clear message when any of these hold: no password hash configured; malformed PHC string; Argon2id params below the pinned minimums (m=19456, t=2, p=1); daemon URL not http:// literal loopback.
- [ ] wallet-web init writes the config 0600, verified after a run under umask 000.
- [ ] init rejects a password under 12 chars, and rejects >1024-byte input BEFORE hashing.
- [ ] Every criterion above is covered by a test that runs under the default cargo test.
- [ ] Startup initialises structured tracing at the RUST_LOG-selected level (NOT a wallet-web.toml
      key -- the plan's config inventory is deliberately closed).
- [ ] A grep of the tree finds no log statement carrying the password, session token, bearer token,
      or a full invoice. Runtime log-capture for the AUTH path belongs to br-nfz and for
      invoice-bearing money paths to br-t8f; the final repository-wide audit is br-4yz. This bead
      builds no routes and no auth logic, so it cannot exercise them.
- [ ] Startup rejects an Argon2i AND an Argon2d PHC string even when m/t/p look strong. The plan
      fixes the ALGORITHM as Argon2id; testing only malformed strings and weak parameters leaves a
      strong-looking wrong-family hash passing every listed check.
- [ ] Oversized password input is proven to reach NO hashing operation at all, rather than merely
      being rejected after the fact.
- [ ] `nix build` succeeds with the new crate present, proving flake.nix's rustSrc paths were
      updated alongside the workspace members list.
- [ ] The daemon-URL test names `http://localhost:9736` explicitly and asserts it is REJECTED. A
      suite that only rejects e.g. `http://192.168.1.5` passes while an implementation that
      resolves-and-accepts `localhost` ships — and `localhost` is the URL an operator would most
      naturally type, which is why item 3 was sharpened to exclude it.
close_reason: Merged to main as 0b21647 (PR #29). wallet-web crate skeleton, config, wallet-web init, and fail-closed startup. Every acceptance criterion is covered by a test running under the default cargo test (25 in wallet-web) and was additionally verified against the built binary: binds 127.0.0.1 only and answers 404 from the empty router; init through a pty writes 0600; and each refusal exits non-zero. Gates green: fmt --check, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings, test --workspace 740 passed, nix build. Item 11 of br-nfz (session-timeout ceilings) landed here; zeroize and any further public_origin work are recorded as deferred on br-nfz.

title: wallet-web: money surface (send, receive+QR, move, direct-inflow)
description:
`wallet-web` money surface: send, receive with server-side QR, move, direct-inflow.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.3, §6c.5 (including "Idempotency and double-submit" and
"Money form contracts"). Depends on the read surface.

MONEY-CRITICAL. `ReceiveRequest.nonce` and `MoveRequest.occurrence` are CLIENT-SUPPLIED idempotency
inputs: a refresh or resubmit that regenerates them is admitted by the daemon as a SECOND money
operation. A JS button-disable is not a defence — the spec requires the UI to work without JS.

Required:
1. Every money form GENERATES ITS IDEMPOTENCY VALUE AT RENDER TIME into a hidden field, so a
   resubmit of the same rendered form carries the same key and dedupes at the daemon. Preserve it
   through preview/confirm/retry.
2. Pay and Move use Post/Redirect/Get so a refresh re-issues a GET. Receive and DirectInflow do
   NOT redirect -- their invoice exists only in the POST response body and a browser does not
   render a redirect's body, so they render the result in place. That is safe because the
   idempotency key is fixed at render time and the daemon re-yields the same invoice. Do NOT store
   transient result state in the sidecar to work around this.
2b. Snapshot policy-derived fields into the form. The idempotency value alone does NOT guarantee
   replay: when federation or fee cap are unset the daemon resolves them from CURRENT policy per
   POST, and for a move the resolved fee cap is an INPUT TO THE OPERATION KEY
   (handlers.rs: `let fee_cap = request.fee_cap.unwrap_or(policy.max_fee)` feeding `move_key`).
   A policy edit between the first POST and a retry then yields a different key from the same
   occurrence and admits a SECOND move. Each rendered form must submit EXPLICIT federation and
   fee-cap values.
3. Send: paste a BOLT11 invoice, show a decoded preview (amount, destination, expiry) BEFORE
   submit, allow a fee cap, confirm, POST /v1/pay.
4. Receive and DirectInflow return their payable invoice ONLY in the POST response. Redirecting
   straight to the operation page would discard it — render a RESULT PAGE carrying the invoice, its
   server-rendered QR, the operation key, and a link to the detail page. Re-attaching the same
   receive key re-yields the same invoice, which also fixes refresh-loses-the-invoice.
5. QR rendered SERVER-SIDE as inline SVG (`qrcode` crate). No JS QR library, no external service.
6. Move (/v1/move) and DirectInflow (/v1/direct-inflow) forms.
7. Per-form contract: which federation (selector where the DTO accepts one, defaulted to the policy
   spending pin), which fields are optional, and units. **Amounts are exact decimal sats with at
   most three fractional digits, converted to integer msat WITHOUT floating point.** Never parse an
   amount into f64.
8. Operations here are `Actor::User` — no Actor enum change.
9. Pay is async and may settle hours later (ADR-0024). The UI must never imply settlement because
   the POST returned 2xx.

Tests: malformed invoice rejected before submit; decoded preview matches the invoice; QR payload
equals the invoice string; **submitting the same rendered receive/move form twice WITH JAVASCRIPT
DISABLED produces exactly ONE operation -- and the Move case MUST edit `max_fee` between the two
submissions and still yield ONE operation**, since a test that does not touch policy passes even
when the form omits the cap and lets the daemon re-derive it into a different `move_key` (which is
the whole defect); likewise assert Receive keeps its snapshotted federation and cap across a policy
edit; the same receive key re-yields the same invoice; result page carries invoice+QR.

Scope guard: no LNURL, no Lightning Address, no on-chain, no amountless invoices. No retry, fallback
or route logic in the frontend — the engine owns that. Never re-sum fees client-side.

Copy canon (roadmap-to-v1.md 6b notes) applies to every string this bead renders: never use "risk
engine", "safe", "bank", "mint" as a verb, "curated", or "anonymous". Amounts display in sats with
msat precision where non-zero. Agent and evacuation actions are described money-centric,
past-tense, with reasons.
10. RENDER MONEY FORMS DISABLED when the daemon is unreachable, using br-pfc's shared
    degraded-state contract, with an explanation rather than failing on submit. br-4yz verifies
    this end to end; the implementation is owned HERE.
11. DirectInflow carries its OWN client nonce (`DirectInflowRequest.nonce`, wallet-api/src/lib.rs:271),
    so it is subject to the identical render-time idempotency rule as Receive. Do not treat it as a
    lesser sibling of the receive flow.
12. THE TEST DAEMON MUST USE THE REAL KEY DERIVATION. "Exactly ONE operation" and "the same
    receive key re-yields the same invoice" are DAEMON-side behaviours, and a real invoice needs a
    live federation, so these tests necessarily run against a fake daemon. That fake MUST compute
    admission keys by calling the actual functions -- `move_key`, `direct_inflow_nonce_key`,
    `raw_receive_key` (all `pub` in `wallet-fedimint`, already imported at handlers.rs:29) -- and
    For POLICY RESOLUTION the real function is NOT importable -- `resolve_fed` is a private fn in
    `wallet-daemon`, which is a binary-only crate with no lib.rs -- so the fake must instead
    replicate the two-line rule EXPLICITLY and cite it: fee_cap = request.fee_cap OR
    policy.max_fee; to = request.to OR policy.spending_fed (handlers.rs:335-336, :305/:374/:398).
    Do not refactor the daemon to expose it: that would breach the one-daemon-change budget.
    A natural fake that dedupes on `occurrence`/`nonce` alone NULLIFIES the whole suite: the
    max_fee-edit test then passes against exactly the broken form it exists to catch, because the
    fake never feeds the cap into the key. This is the single highest user-visible risk of the
    phase, and the test's apparent rigor would otherwise manufacture false confidence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A malformed invoice is rejected before submission, and the decoded preview (amount, destination, expiry) matches the invoice.
- [ ] Receive renders a server-side SVG QR whose payload equals the invoice string exactly.
- [ ] Submitting the same rendered receive form twice WITH JAVASCRIPT DISABLED yields exactly ONE operation and the same invoice.
- [ ] Submitting the same rendered move form twice WITH JAVASCRIPT DISABLED yields exactly ONE operation EVEN WHEN max_fee IS EDITED BETWEEN THE TWO SUBMISSIONS. A test that does not change policy between submissions passes against the broken implementation too and therefore proves nothing.
- [ ] Receive keeps its snapshotted federation and fee cap across a policy edit.
- [ ] Pay and Move redirect after POST; Receive and DirectInflow render their result in place, because the invoice exists only in the POST body. No transient result state is stored in the sidecar.
- [ ] Amounts are parsed as exact decimal sats to integer msat with no floating point anywhere in the path.
- [ ] The UI never implies a payment settled merely because the POST returned 2xx.
- [ ] Every user-facing string this bead adds conforms to the copy canon.
- [ ] Submitting the same rendered DIRECTINFLOW form twice WITH JAVASCRIPT DISABLED yields exactly
      ONE operation and the same invoice, and its result page carries the invoice, QR, operation key
      and detail link. Testing only Receive and Move leaves this duplicate-money path unproven.
- [ ] Amount conversion is proven by a boundary table, not a token case: 1 sat; 1.001 sat; 0.001 sat;
      more than three fractional digits REJECTED; malformed input REJECTED; a value large enough to
      overflow REJECTED. Each accepted case yields the exact integer msat with no floating point
      anywhere in the path, so a 1000x units error cannot pass.
- [ ] Money forms render disabled (not failing-on-submit) when the daemon is unreachable.
- [ ] DirectInflow replay under POLICY MUTATION: render once, submit, then change BOTH the spending
      pin and max_fee, resubmit the identical rendered form with JS disabled, and assert ONE
      operation, the same invoice, and the ORIGINAL destination and cap. `DirectInflowRequest.to` is
      Option and the handler resolves policy.spending_fed before keying (handlers.rs:391), so a form
      omitting it passes an unchanged-policy test and duplicates after a pin change.
- [ ] Pay's rendered request also carries explicit federation and fee cap: the snapshot rule is for
      EVERY money form, not only those with an obvious nonce.
- [ ] Log capture over a SUCCESSFUL and a FAILING daemon call proves no full invoice and no bearer
      token is emitted at any level; a static grep misses structured logging of a request object.
- [ ] The test daemon calls the real `move_key` / `direct_inflow_nonce_key` / `raw_receive_key`;
      re-implementing THOSE is a defect. Policy resolution is the stated exception -- `resolve_fed`
      is private to a binary-only crate, so requirement 12's explicit two-line replica IS the
      mandated approach there, not a shortcut.
- [ ] Prove the harness is not vacuous: with the FORM deliberately broken (omitting the fee cap so
      the daemon re-derives it), the max_fee-edit test must FAIL. A suite that stays green against
      that form is testing nothing.
- [ ] The fake ALSO models live-attach sizing validation, not only key derivation: `raw_receive_key`
      omits the fee cap while `validate_live_attach` COMPARES it (wallet-fedimint/src/service/actor.rs
      ~2140-2173). A fake deduping on the key alone re-yields the invoice and passes the
      policy-mutation test while the real walletd returns a sizing conflict. Prove non-vacuity: the
      deliberately-broken form must make this test FAIL.

title: Fail-fast (503) on fresh dest-side requests to joined-but-unopened federations
description:
## Outcome
A FRESH `/v1/receive`, `/v1/direct-inflow`, or move whose destination is joined but not
currently open returns an explicit unavailable (503) at admission, instead of being admitted,
parking Pending, and (for receive/direct-inflow) stalling ~30s before a 504.

## Why this exists
Surfaced by a review bot on PR #1 and analyzed by two independent models (codex gpt-5.6-sol +
fable) plus local verification. The bot's framing was mostly WRONG and is NOT a defect (see
Non-goals), but both models independently identified one genuine, minor residue worth a
follow-up: the current path is a UX/liveness wart, not a bug.

Today: `sample_balances` (wallet-daemon/src/handlers.rs:651) omits an unopened fed, admission
treats its balance as zero and journals the op; the driver then fails closed (Retryable ->
Pending) and the watch scheduler retries `open_all` every cycle, so it self-heals when the fed
opens. For receive/direct-inflow the caller waits on `block_for_invoice` up to ~30s and gets a
504 (handlers.rs:599/638) rather than an instant 503. A fed that NEVER opens leaves an immortal
Pending row holding reservations (executor.rs:83/103/139/166) — liveness/capacity pressure, not
stranded money.

## Scope
An admission-time openness check for FRESH destination-side requests only, returning 503.

## Non-goals / must-preserve (critical — both models flagged this)
- NOT a blanket precheck in the handlers. Existing Pending/Awaiting/completed idempotent
  requests MUST remain attachable, and an already-created invoice MUST remain retrievable even
  if the destination is temporarily closed (durable journal state, actor.rs:1621/1632). A naive
  unconditional check breaks attach + idempotent replay.
- Does NOT reverse the park-and-retry design. Project history records that a general
  "unopened-fed pre-check" was reviewed and REJECTED in phase-6a step-5 as forbidden
  new-handling with no money-loss. This bead is narrower: fail-fast for FRESH requests only,
  preserving attach/retrieval — not an admission refusal for all cases.
- No money-safety change: nothing is debited before the destination opens (verified: receive/
  inflow debit no source; in a move CreateInvoice precedes Pay and needs dest-side calls that
  fail Retryable while closed, executor.rs:1175 before :1309).

## Critical constraints
Distinguish FRESH from EXISTING intent at admission (nonce/key lookup) before returning 503.
Consider also terminalizing or GC-ing immortal Pending rows for feds that never open (separate
concern; may be its own bead).

## Dependencies / ordering
Independent. Pre-existing behavior (sample_balances, since commit 4aaef17); not blocked by
anything.

## Verification
- Unit/integration: a FRESH receive/direct-inflow/move to a joined-but-unopened dest returns
  503 (not admitted, not a 30s-504); an EXISTING Pending/Awaiting intent for the same key still
  attaches; an already-minted invoice is still retrievable while the dest is briefly closed.
- Regression: the existing `tests.rs:275` behavior (joined-but-unopened -> admitted -> 504) is
  intentionally CHANGED for the fresh case; update it and assert the attach/retrieval paths.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Fresh dest-side request to an unopened fed returns 503 with an actionable message.
- [ ] Existing-intent attach and invoice retrieval are preserved (tested).
- [ ] The park-and-retry / self-heal path for already-admitted intents is untouched.
- [ ] `cargo test && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check` pass.

title: wallet-web: federation, admin, policy, diagnostics surfaces
description:
`wallet-web` federation, admin, policy, and diagnostics surfaces.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.3, §6c.5. Depends on the read surface.

Required:
1. Federations: join (/v1/join), candidates (/v1/candidates), approve (/v1/approve).
2. Admin: reconcile (/v1/reconcile), recover (/v1/recover).
3. **Diagnostics panel** surfacing /v1/status, /v1/watch/status and /v1/health (scheduler alive,
   watch state, daemon health). These are part of the "full parity" claim and previously had no
   page and no bead — that was a coverage gap.
4. Policy view + edit. **Read-modify-write, never reconstruct**: `PUT /v1/policy` takes a WHOLE
   `Policy`, and new policy fields ship `#[serde(default)]`, so a form that rebuilds `Policy` from
   only the fields it knows would SILENTLY RESET any field added later — including money caps. GET
   the current policy, merge the edited fields into that value, PUT the result.
5. Policy edits state units explicitly (msat vs bps). The runbook's cap arithmetic was previously
   wrong precisely because units were ambiguous.
6. Every destructive/irreversible action — recover, approve, join, policy edits — requires an
   explicit CONFIRMATION STEP on a separate page naming in plain language what will happen.
   `recover` re-seeds a wallet; `approve` decides which federations become fundable (the trust
   decision ADR-0017's probe gate protects). This is a UI affordance, NOT an auth gate: ADR-0028
   chose no step-up and this must not smuggle one back in.
7. The seed/mnemonic is NEVER exposed by any route to any session. Seed export stays CLI-only and
   daemon-stopped (runbook Day 0).

Tests: each destructive action requires passing its confirmation page; **a policy round-trip
preserves a field the form does not know about** (prove read-modify-write, not reconstruct); no
route returns seed material; diagnostics render.

Scope guard: no multi-user, no roles, no new daemon endpoints. No policy validation logic in the
frontend — submit and render what the daemon says.

Copy canon (roadmap-to-v1.md 6b notes) applies to every string this bead renders: never use "risk
engine", "safe", "bank", "mint" as a verb, "curated", or "anonymous". Amounts display in sats with
msat precision where non-zero. Agent and evacuation actions are described money-centric,
past-tense, with reasons.
This matters most on the confirmation pages, which must name the real consequence in plain language
rather than reassuring the user.
8. RENDER ADMIN AND POLICY FORMS DISABLED when the daemon is unreachable, using br-pfc's shared
   degraded-state contract, with an explanation rather than failing on submit.
9. STATE THE CONFIRMATION CONTRACT MECHANICALLY. It is a UI affordance, NOT an auth gate
   (ADR-0028 chose no step-up): the mutating form for recover/approve/join/policy-PUT is RENDERED
   ONLY on its confirmation page, which names the consequence in plain language. The test asserts
   the two-step flow and the page's content. It must NOT assert that a direct POST carrying valid
   CSRF is rejected -- that would be the step-up gate the ADR excluded, and testing it as a
   rejection would silently reintroduce one.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Join, approve, candidates, reconcile, recover and policy view/edit are reachable and function against the daemon.
- [ ] Every destructive or irreversible action (recover, approve, join, policy edit) requires passing an explicit confirmation page that names the consequence in plain language.
- [ ] A policy edit preserves a field the form does not know about, proving read-modify-write rather than reconstruct. Rebuilding Policy from known fields would silently reset serde-default fields including money caps.
- [ ] Policy units are stated explicitly (msat vs bps) on every editable field.
- [ ] The diagnostics panel surfaces /v1/status, /v1/watch/status and /v1/health.
- [ ] No route returns seed or mnemonic material under any circumstance.
- [ ] Every user-facing string this bead adds conforms to the copy canon, and each confirmation
      page names the actual consequence rather than reassuring.
- [ ] Admin and policy forms render disabled (not failing-on-submit) when the daemon is unreachable.
- [ ] The two-step flow and confirmation-page content are asserted; a direct POST with valid CSRF
      is NOT asserted to fail (that would be a step-up gate ADR-0028 excluded).

title: Evacuate: base + proportional fee cap (absolute cap cannot fund a real evacuation)
description:
Give `Evacuate` a base + proportional fee cap so a full-balance evacuation is not refused on price.

Authority: [ADR-0029](docs/adr/0029-evacuation-must-be-executable.md). Amends
[ADR-0018](docs/adr/0018-v1-evacuation-balance-cap.md), whose balance cap still stands.

## The problem

`wallet-core/src/allocator.rs` builds the `Evacuate` action with `fee_cap: snapshot.max_fee` — the
single ABSOLUTE cap — immediately beneath a comment stating "Route economics NEVER gates an
evacuation -- a dying federation must be drained even when the route prices badly". The parameter
contradicts the intent it sits under.

At the runbook's suggested settings, with fees measured on the pilot gateway:
- per-federation cap 75,000,000 msat
- measured swap cost at 1,000,000 msat: send 8,948 + receive 8,900 = 17,848 (1.78%)
- the same rate on a full federation: ~1,338,600 msat
- `--max-fee` absolute cap: 50,000 msat
- **over cap by ~27x**, and the consequence depends on the gateway's FEE SHAPE. Two distinct
  failure modes, both real, established by reading `size_fresh_evacuation` (executor.rs:606-667),
  the fit predicate (executor.rs:814-829) and `total_within_cap` (fee.rs:160-164) -- which sums
  BOTH legs' quotes, each INCLUDING the gateway's base fee, against the cap:
  1. BASE FEES BELOW THE CAP -> CHUNK-DRAIN. A smaller net fits, so the evacuation is silently
     downsized (warning at :654-663). The occurrence advances every watch cycle
     (scheduler.rs:692-697) and `idem_evac` embeds it (allocator.rs:629), so a fresh Evacuate is
     emitted for the remainder and the balance drains in ~27 chunks at ~the same total fee. This
     is what the pilot's MEASURED gateway does.
  2. NO AMOUNT FITS -> GENUINE REFUSAL. The condition is about the WHOLE SEARCH: a single quote
      strictly above the cap rejects THAT AMOUNT and sizing downsizes; refusal comes only after
      every amount has failed (CONTEXT.md's **Serves**: "only 'no amount fits' is a failure"). The
      per-quote test underneath is that a summed two-leg quote strictly above the cap fails. State
      that test about the QUOTE:
      `total_within_cap` is `receive_quote + send_quote <= fee_cap` (`fee.rs:163`), so exact
      equality EXECUTES and only cap-plus-one-msat refuses. For bases specifically: bases summing
      to exactly the cap still refuse once any ppm/federation/mint component is nonzero, because
      the comparison is on the total. A base does not shrink with the amount, so
     if the two bases alone exceed fee_cap, NO candidate ever fits and the executor returns
     `Retryable` (:646-653) every tick -- a silent livelock, not a terminal failure. A gateway may
     charge bases summing to ~150 sats against the runbook's 50-sat cap, so this is reachable.
  An earlier draft of this bead claimed (1) is the only behaviour and refusal is impossible. That
  was wrong; do not reintroduce it. The fix addresses both: one operation instead of ~27, a faster
  exit from a dying federation, and no silent livelock when a gateway's base is high.

No evacuation has ever run in production, so this has never been observed. `Move` is unaffected:
it already uses a proportional cap (`move_fee_cap(amount, snapshot.max_fee_bps_of_move)`).

A flat percentage would fail at the opposite end. The gateway's INTENDED envelope is `SEND_FEE_LIMIT` (100 sats + 1.5%) plus
`RECEIVE_FEE_LIMIT` (50 sats + 0.5%) ~= 150 sats + 2%. Do NOT call this a protocol bound: at our
pinned SDK rev it is not enforced, because `PaymentFee` derives a lexicographic `PartialOrd` over
(base, parts_per_million) and the check is a single `.le(...)`, so a small base with an arbitrarily
large ppm passes (the upstream defect this project reported separately). Nor does it bound the
wallet's total cost, which also includes federation and mint-note fees. OUR cap is the only real
bound, which is exactly why its shape matters. Treat 200+3% as a pilot starting point; the base component
dominates at small amounts, so a legitimate worst case is 2.2% of a 75,000-sat evacuation but 17%
of a 1,000-sat one. Hence base + proportional.

## Required changes

1. Add an evacuation fee cap of the form `base + proportional`, defaulting to **200 sats + 3%**
   (chosen to sit above the ~150 sats + 2% envelope gateways are INTENDED to advertise, with
   headroom at every size). That envelope is not a protocol worst case and not a total-cost
   bound: nothing enforces it on a gateway, and federation receive/send fees and mint-note fees
   apply on top -- see ADR-0029, which makes the same point. The defaults are a calibrated
   starting point; the CAP is the enforcement, not the envelope. Both components
   configurable through `Policy` alongside the existing knobs. In FIELD UNITS the defaults are
   `evac_fee_base_msat = 200_000` and `evac_fee_bps = 300` -- write them that way, matching the
   runbook's existing `--max-fee-bps-of-move 300` for 3%.
1b. THE EXACT ARITHMETIC, so two implementers cannot diverge:
      cap_msat = base_msat + floor(executed_net_msat * bps / 10_000)
    FLOOR, matching the existing proportional policy (`allocator.rs:153`). Compute in u128 (or
    checked u64) and saturate rather than wrap. At 1_000_001 msat net, floor gives 230_000 and
    ceil would give 230_001; a 230_001-msat quote must be REFUSED.
    THE CAP'S BASE IS THE EXECUTED NET. That is deliberately NOT the base the SDK charges on:
    the gateway's receive fee is charged on the gross invoice (`fee.rs:10`) and the send fee on
    the invoice / outgoing contract (`executor.rs:849`). Applying 3% to a 1_100_000-msat invoice
    yields 233_000 instead of the required 230_000. Tests must derive the CAP from net while
    deriving each CHARGED fee from its real SDK base.
2. `Evacuate`'s `fee_cap` is computed from that, NOT from `snapshot.max_fee`. Leave `Move` on
   `move_fee_cap(...)` untouched.
2b. The cap must bound the FINAL EXECUTED net, not the planned amount, AND survive replay.
   Today `fee_cap` is a single collapsed `Msat` on `Action::Evacuate`, `MovePlan`, `MoveParams` and
   `MoveRecord` (wallet-core/src/types.rs:490, move_protocol.rs:80, :98), so the executor cannot
   recompute base + bps x executed from it -- the (base, bps) COMPONENTS must travel to wherever
   the recompute happens. THIS BEAD DECIDES IT; do not re-open it during implementation:
     (a) The (base, bps) components are SNAPSHOTTED onto `Action::Evacuate` by `decide()`, exactly
         as the admitted parameters they are, and travel through `MovePlan`/`MoveParams`.
     (b) The FINAL recomputed cap is committed into the receive operation's `MoveMeta`, beside the
         clamped `amount` it already persists (`move_protocol.rs:188-202`) -- the same crash-safe
         channel, written in the same place, recovered by the same path.
         THE FIELD IS `Option<Msat>`, MARKED `#[serde(default)]`, AND ABSENT MEANS `None` -- NOT
         a zero cap. Write `cap: Msat` with a plain `#[serde(default)]` and every pre-change row
         decodes to a 0-msat cap; (c) below PREFERS the `MoveMeta` cap over `params.fee_cap`, and
         `pay_step_cap_verdict` (`executor.rs:2009-2014`) classifies a fixed receive quote over
         the cap as PERMANENT -- so an in-flight pre-upgrade move with a committed receive is
         TERMINALLY FAILED by the upgrade. `None` falls back to `params.fee_cap`. This is the
         same trap §3 names for `Policy`, and it is worse here because the row is a payment.
         AC: a legacy-`MoveMeta` fixture (a row encoded WITHOUT the field) decodes to `None`,
         falls back, and completes -- the analogue of §2e's legacy-intent replay test.
         `MoveMeta` rides committed SDK op metas and the
         journal, both LIVE PRODUCTION STORES with rows written by the running daemon, so a
         non-defaulted field fails to decode every pre-change row -- and unlike a policy row, a
         move record cannot be re-created by re-running a command. This is the same granted
         forward-compat exception as the Policy fields, for the same reason; the scope guard's
         "the `#[serde(default)]` allowance above is the only compatibility concession" means the
         only KIND of concession, not the only field. A decoded-as-default cap on an old row is
         correct behaviour: those moves were planned under the absolute cap and carry no
         recomputed value.
     (c) Reassembly PREFERS the `MoveMeta` cap over `params.fee_cap` (today `assemble_move_record`
         takes params unconditionally, `move_protocol.rs:428`). `params.fee_cap` remains the
         planning value and the pre-execution bound.
   REJECTED alternative, and why, so it is not revived: re-deriving the cap from a plumbed live
   `Policy` at execution time. An operator running `policy set` mid-flight would retroactively
   shrink an in-flight evacuation's cap, and `pay_step_cap_verdict` is PERMANENT when the fixed
   receive quote alone exceeds the cap (`executor.rs:2009-2014`) -- so a routine policy edit could
   terminally kill an evacuation whose invoice is already minted. It also violates the immutable
   admitted-parameters rule (`docs/phase6a-plan.md:325`).
   Crash safety is the money-critical half: replay reconstructs `MoveParams.fee_cap` from the
   original plan (executor.rs:264) and `assemble_move_record` treats params as authoritative,
   overwriting the cached `fee_cap` (move_protocol.rs:297, :418), while `MoveMeta` persists the
   downsized AMOUNT but not its cap (move_protocol.rs:187). So after a receive commit plus cache
   loss, replay can restore the PLANNED-amount cap and authorise an excessive fee on the smaller
   executed net. That is what 2b(a)-(c) above closes; this paragraph records the hazard, not an
   open question.
   The underlying hazard: The allocator fixes
   `Action::Evacuate.fee_cap` before execution (allocator.rs:558-626) while the executor may
   still clamp to a smaller net (executor.rs:629-665, 715-769) without recomputing it. A
   compliant-looking implementation could plan 75,000 sats, keep the matching cap, get clamped to
   1,000 sats, and permit a fee far above base + 3% of what actually moved. Recompute (or
   re-verify) the cap against the executed amount and persist the result.
2c. SIZING: AN AMOUNT-DEPENDENT CAP IS NOT MONOTONE, AND THE BISECTION ASSUMES IT IS.
   `largest_fitting_amount` is a strict bisection whose contract is stated in its own doc: "The
   CALLER owns the monotonicity argument: `fits` must be fits-then-doesn't as the amount grows"
   (`executor.rs:1661-1664`). `max_affordable_evacuation_net` currently earns that by clamping the
   search to `[MINIMUM_INCOMING_CONTRACT_MSAT, desired]` (`executor.rs:718-727`) -- which fixes the
   too-small end ONLY. A constant cap keeps the predicate monotone. `cap(a) = base + bps*a` does
   NOT: when a gateway's bases exceed the cap base while its ppm is below the rate, feasibility
   INCREASES with amount, so the feasible set is a MIDDLE WINDOW and one false probe below it
   discards everything above.
   Worked case that must not regress -- RE-DERIVED with EXECUTABLE bases, because bases summing
   400 sats cannot occur at the pin (send > 100 or receive > 50 is refused; an earlier revision
   fixtured 400 and the assertion "the evacuation still proceeds" was unreachable):
   gateway bases 99 + 49 = 148 sats, combined ppm 5,000 (0.5%), cap configured to 20 sats +
   300 bps, source balance 10,000 sats. NOTE this regime needs an operator-configured LOW cap
   base: at the 200-sat default no executable base can exceed it (the ceiling is
   150 sats -- `.le` admits equality, so 100 + 50 is executable for a gateway keeping its ppm
   within the nominal limits; ~148 is the ceiling only for the arbitrary-ppm hostile shape), so the increasing
   regime is unreachable and the guard untestable. The cap constraint needs a >= ~5,120 sats and
   spendable allows a <= ~9,800 sats, so ~9,500 sats IS affordable -- but the fast path fails and
   the first probe at ~5,002 sats has fee ~173 sats > cap ~170 sats, collapsing `hi` to 5,001 and
   discarding the whole window. Result `Ok(None)` -> `ExecError::Retryable` (`executor.rs:646-653`)
   every tick forever: the EXACT livelock this bead exists to kill, reintroduced by its own fix.
   THE PREDICATE IS NOT MONOTONE, AND MAKING IT MONOTONE IS NOT THE FIX.
   Writing `fee(a) - cap(a) = (bases - base) + (ppm_total - bps_rate) * a`, the slope can go
   either way, so the feasible set is a TOP window (bases > base, ppm < bps) or a BOTTOM window
   (bases < base, ppm > bps). Worse, every term floors independently -- gateway
   (`base + floor(ppm*a/1e6)`, fee.rs:47-57), lnv2 module and mint module (same shape, ppm capped
   at 1_000 by the constructor, `fedimint-lnv2-common/src/config.rs:62-107`,
   `fedimint-mint-common/src/config.rs:66-78`), and the cap itself -- so around the crossing the
   verdict genuinely oscillates. It is NOT a clean interval there: measured 29_100 components in
   the adversarial fixture below.

   THE KEY OBSERVATION, and the reason this does not need an exhaustive search: in the
   oscillating band every fitting amount fits with ~ZERO SLACK, and a zero-slack fit MAY NOT
   SURVIVE THE PAY-STEP RE-QUOTE (it DOES when the fee inputs are unchanged -- equality is
   admitted; the point is that it has no margin, not that it fails) -- `pay_step_cap_verdict` re-checks against a fresh quote whose
   drift is of the same magnitude. Chasing msat-exact fits buys a candidate that fails later.
   So sizing owes completeness only up to a slack margin, not to the msat.

   REQUIRED:
   (a) TWO PASSES. A single bisection on the combined predicate is NOT sufficient, and must not
       be prescribed: it is exactly what the worked case above defeats. There the fast probe at
       `T = desired` fails on AFFORDABILITY (the full balance cannot fund itself), and a combined
       bisection then probes ~5,002 sats, fails on the CAP, and discards the feasible window
       [~5,120, ~9,802] entirely. That window is not knife-edge -- at 9,000 sats fee ~193 vs cap
       ~290 is ~97 SATS of slack -- comfortably above the `2A` threshold in (b) (`2A` is
       ~5,800 msat at fewest tiers, ~18,000 msat at eleven). So the slack argument does NOT
       explain why the window is missed, and must not be offered as the reason: an earlier
       revision claimed "25 sats, only ~1.4x-5x 2A", which was computed under the RETIRED
       bases-400 fixture. The window is missed STRUCTURALLY -- a combined bisection probes below
       the window bottom and collapses `hi` -- and pass 1's affordability-only bisection finds it
       regardless. That is the whole argument; the margin is irrelevant to it. It is a structural miss.
         PASS 1 -- bisect on the affordability constraint ALONE
         (`source_debit(a) <= spendable`) over `[MINIMUM_INCOMING_CONTRACT_MSAT, T]`, then check
         the cap AT that result.
         AFFORDABILITY IS NOT STRICTLY MONOTONE, and an earlier revision of this bead asserted it
         was ("monotone by construction"). It is not: mint fees are per input and per output, so
         the note COUNT enters `source_debit`, and raising the requested amount can cross a
         note-selection or change boundary that REDUCES the input/change count and therefore
         LOWERS `source_debit`. An unaffordable quote can be followed by an affordable one, and a
         plain bisection can collapse `hi` onto a discontinuity and discard a feasible upper
         interval -- leaving the evacuation retrying forever with an affordable amount available.
         So pass 1 carries the SAME robustness treatment pass 2 already has: when the probe fails
         by at most the oscillation bound `A` (`shortfall <= A`, equality included), probe candidates
         above it before collapsing `hi`, on the DETERMINISTIC SCHEDULE defined once below. The
         bound is the same `A`; the direction is the mirror, because here the discontinuity can
         make a LARGER amount fit.
         AC: a fixture whose mint inventory crosses a note-count boundary inside `[floor, T]`, in
         which the naive bisection discards the feasible interval and the robust one does not. This
         is what finds the TOP window: in the worked case it lands on ~9,802 sats, where fee ~197
         vs cap ~314 fits.
         PASS 2 -- only if the cap fails at pass 1's result: bisect the COMBINED predicate over
         `[MINIMUM_INCOMING_CONTRACT_MSAT, pass1_result]`. In the decreasing regime that reaches
         this branch, `fee - cap` is increasing in `a`, so the combined predicate IS
         fits-then-doesn't and the contract holds. This finds the BOTTOM window. In the
         increasing regime pass 2 harmlessly finds nothing, because pass 1 already ruled it out.
         Refuse only when BOTH passes fail.
       `T = min(desired, destination cap room)`, and BOTH passes are bounded above by it:
       `desired` is already clamped to destination cap room (`clamp_desired_to_cap_room`,
       executor.rs:673-692) and evacuations are EXEMPT from `enforce_destination_cap`
       (executor.rs:1312-1314), so an unbounded search can size an evacuation clean over the
       ADR-0018 hard cap with nothing downstream to catch it.
   (b) REWRITE `largest_fitting_amount`'s contract (executor.rs:1660-1664) from monotonicity --
       which the amount-dependent cap genuinely breaks -- to ROBUSTNESS:
         "Returns a probed-fitting amount at least as large as every amount the BOUNDED probe
          reaches; this is best-effort, NOT "every amount that fits with 2A
          msat of slack. Returns None only when no such amount exists."
       `A` is the oscillation bound, computed AT STARTUP from the mint tier count and the
       consolidation bound -- AND THE MINT'S PROPORTIONAL PER-NOTE FEE, which an earlier revision
       omitted: `A ~= 6 + 2*(300*#tiers + 100) + 2_100 + 2*ceil(V_max * mint_ppm / 1e6)` msat,
       where `V_max` bounds the value of a single selected input or change note. The pinned
       mint's per-note fee is `base + floor(note_amount * ppm / 1_000_000)`, so at a
       note-selection boundary the fee discontinuity SCALES WITH THE DENOMINATION crossed. A
       tier-count-only `A` can be smaller than a real jump by orders of magnitude, and the
       `shortfall <= A` probe rules in (a) and (b) then refuse immediately without probing a
       nearby viable amount -- the failure those rules exist to prevent. If `V_max` cannot be
       bounded at startup, derive `A` per-search from the actual selected notes rather than
       pretending a constant covers it.
       THE PROBE SCHEDULE, DEFINED ONCE AND REFERENCED BY BOTH PASSES. "A bounded number of
       candidates" is NOT a specification, and ADR-0029 rejects that wording: `A` bounds the
       VERTICAL fee jump, not the HORIZONTAL distance to the next note-selection discontinuity, so
       an implementation can obey the words, probe the wrong offsets, miss an executable amount
       and strand the evacuation. REQUIRED, AS BOUNDED BEST-EFFORT -- NOT completeness: probe the
       NOTE-SELECTION BOUNDARIES adjacent to the failing candidate, derived from the mint tier
       denominations rather than guessed offsets, for a stated maximum count (start at 8 per
       direction), stopping at the first candidate that fits. ADR-0029 explicitly ACCEPTS that a
       feasible window lying beyond more boundaries than are visited is MISSED and the evacuation
       keeps retrying; do NOT state or test a "finds every amount that fits with 2A of slack"
       property -- a bounded probe cannot deliver it, since `A` bounds one vertical jump and not
       the count or spacing of them. State the count and the boundary derivation in the implementation, and
       cover it with a fixture whose feasible amount sits exactly one boundary away from the
       failing probe: without the schedule that fixture must go red.
       WHAT THE TWO PASSES ACTUALLY LEAVE OUT, so the contract is not read as covering more than
       it does: structural windows are found by pass 1 or pass 2. What remains uncovered is the
       OSCILLATION near the crossing, where floor jitter can flip the verdict msat to msat. The
       contract is not a weakening of the search; it names the residue the search is not OBLIGED
       to chase.
       DO NOT read this as "zero-slack amounts are unusable". They are not: `total_within_cap`
       compares with `<=` (`fee.rs:160-164`), so an exact-cap candidate is ADMITTED, and when the
       fee inputs are unchanged between sizing and Pay it survives the re-quote intact. The
       exact-cap acceptance criterion below depends on exactly that and is NOT in tension with
       this contract. What the slack argument justifies is only that the SEARCH need not hunt
       through the oscillating band to find such an amount -- not that finding one is useless, and
       not that the comparison acquires a safety margin. Adding a margin to `total_within_cap`
       would be a policy change and is out of scope here.
   (b-bis) ECONOMIC VIABILITY, and this is money-critical: after the search returns its largest
       fitting net `n*`, REJECT THE ROUTE unless the quoted `total_fee <= n*`. Re-check the same
       inequality at the Pay step, and classify a failure there the way the existing cap check
       classifies its own: `pay_step_cap_verdict`'s rules apply unchanged, so a fixed receive
       quote that alone breaks the inequality is PERMANENT, and a send-side breach that a fresh
       attempt could clear stays retryable. Do not invent a third verdict class for this check.
       Why it is needed: the cap's base is amount-independent, so at the 5-sat contract floor a
       200-sat base cap admits a chunk that burns 200 sats to move 5, and the remainder re-emits
       every watch cycle with NO minimum-progress guard, attempt budget or fee accounting. A
       75,000-sat balance drains in ~365 such chunks -- ~1,953 sats delivered, ~73,047 burned, a
       ~97.4% loss. (An earlier revision moved these to 480/2,400/72,600; that was WRONG. The
       sizing search returns the LARGEST fitting net, so at the window top the fee sits at the
       cap, ~200 sats -- never ~150. 480 chunks of 5 sats at 150 each is not a reachable
       parameterisation. The original aggregates were right; only their attribution to a
       "200-sat base" was wrong.) Verified reachable by both reviewers; it needs a hostile or misconfigured
       gateway with COMPLIANT BASES and a hostile ppm -- send base 99 sats, receive base 49 sats.
       The pinned SDK's fee limits do not bound the PPM (the derived `PartialOrd` on `PaymentFee`
       compares `base` first, `gateway_api.rs:190-200`), but they DO bound the bases: send above
       100 sats is refused (`lnv2-client/src/lib.rs:590`), receive above 50 sats at `:905`. So a
       "base just under 200 sats" gateway cannot execute at all -- it strands, it does not burn. On the measured pilot gateway at 1.78% this never fires.
       TWO IMPLEMENTATION CAUTIONS, each of which breaks something if ignored:
         - It is a POST-CHECK on the search RESULT, never a term inside the fits predicate.
           `fee(n) <= n` is false at small `n` and true above `base/(1 - rate)`, so folding it in
           would re-break the fits-then-doesn't monotonicity that 2c depends on.
         - Check the TOP FIRST, but it is NOT sufficient on its own. Efficiency
           `fee(n)/n = base/n + rate` decreases monotonically in `n` for the AFFINE model, so the
           largest fitting amount is the right place to look. The real quote is not affine: the
           two gateway fees, the two federation fees and the per-note MINT fee each floor
           independently, and the note COUNT can change between adjacent amounts, so the fee can
           jump by more than the one-msat gain in `n`. At such a discontinuity the top can fail
           `fee <= n` while a slightly smaller candidate passes.
           REQUIRED: if the top fails by AT MOST the oscillation bound `A` (`shortfall <= A`,
           EQUALITY INCLUDED -- the boundary belongs to the probe, not the refusal), probe candidates
           below it on the DETERMINISTIC SCHEDULE defined once below, before refusing. Refuse only
           when BOTH the top fails by strictly MORE than `A` AND that is an ANALYTICALLY PROVEN
           structural refusal -- `A` bounds ONE discontinuity, so several boundaries can
           cumulatively exceed it with a smaller viable amount still beyond them; a bare
           shortfall over `A` is inconclusive, not proof. Likewise when the probe finds nothing AND that emptiness is an ANALYTICALLY PROVEN
           structural refusal (2c(c)). Probe EXHAUSTION alone is INCONCLUSIVE -- the bounded probe
           is deliberately incomplete, so finding nothing does not prove no viable amount exists:
           stay `Retryable` and do NOT mark the route unavailable or license the dearer hop. A `<` here refuses an
           executable evacuation at exactly `A`. Refusing on a top-only reading would
           discard an executable evacuation. (ADR-0029's Amendment carries the same rule; they
           must not drift apart.)
       A rejected route DOES NOT SERVE, so strict swap-first falls through to the hop (which gets
       the same check, per br-s0e); if neither class serves, the existing `Retryable` refusal
       stands -- stranding rather than burning, per ADR-0018.
       ACCEPTED RESIDUAL: a gateway pricing exactly at `fee == net` still extracts up to half the
       balance across chunks. An aggregate per-evacuation budget would bound that; it is the named
       follow-up, not part of this bead.
   (c) At the `None` site, DISTINGUISH STRUCTURAL FROM INCIDENTAL REFUSAL. Compute the analytic
       slopes -- `s_f` from the two gateway `routing_info` ppms and the four federation ppms
       through the gross-up composition, `s_c = cap_bps / 10_000` -- and emit a
       structural-refusal diagnostic, while staying `Retryable`, under EITHER of TWO conditions.
       Both are needed; an earlier revision had only the first, and it CANNOT FIRE in this
       bead's own livelock fixture:
         (i) `s_c >= s_f` and the largest affordable amount fails the cap -- feasibility rises
             with amount, so nothing SMALLER can help. Cause: "the cap's trend excludes every
             smaller amount; raise evac_fee_base_msat or evac_fee_bps".
        (ii) `s_f >= s_c` AND the COMPLETE MINIMUM FIXED INTERCEPT exceeds `cap_base` -- not the
             gateway bases alone: the cap verdict also carries the fixed lnv2 federation fees and
             the per-note mint component, so gateway bases UNDER the cap base can still sum with
             those to an intercept above it, at which point no amount fits and neither condition
             fires unless (ii) is computed from the full intercept -- then
             `fee(a) - cap(a) = (bases - cap_base) + (s_f - s_c)*a > 0` at EVERY amount and the
             gap only widens, so nothing fits at any size. Cause: "the fixed component alone -- both gateways' bases plus the fixed
             federation and per-note mint fees -- exceeds the cap base; no amount can fit". Do NOT
             word it as "the gateways' bases alone": the condition is computed from the complete
             intercept, so that wording would report a false cause.
       Both are needed: with a low configured cap base and any nonzero fee slope the refusal is
       structural, and (i) alone would not fire. A silent
       indefinite retry is the failure this bead exists to kill; a refusal an operator can act on
       is not.
   (d) The probe budget is small, and stated PER PASS -- not "unchanged": 2c(a) mandates pass 1
       plus a conditional pass 2, and the `shortfall <= A` bounded probes on top, so the worst
       case runs past 100 local quotes, roughly double the single-bisection figure. An implementer
       enforcing ~50 as a HARD search budget truncates pass 2 and refuses an executable evacuation
       -- the livelock class this bead exists to kill. ONE SNAPSHOT PER CANDIDATE: TWO gateway HTTP fetches total (one per leg),
       fetched once and REUSED across both passes -- br-s0e requires this, and re-fetching between
       passes lets the slope move after pass 1 fixed its bound. Only the local dry-run quotes are
       per pass. The fetches are hoisted
       out of the loop
       (`FreshSendRequiredGatewayFees` is passed in, executor.rs:814-829), plus the LOCAL
       dry-run quotes. Verified local: `Client::fee_quote` opens a DB transaction and runs
       `create_final_inputs_and_outputs` against it with no federation request
       (`fedimint-client/src/client.rs:824-900`). Do NOT add batching or a snapshot quote API;
       there is no network cost to amortise.
2d. WARN ON AN OUT-OF-ENVELOPE ADVERTISED PPM -- do NOT reject on it. Log loudly when a gateway
   advertises send ppm > 15_000 or receive ppm > 5_000.
   REJECTING would contradict ADR-0029, whose "Why" section establishes that OUR CAP is the only real bound (the upstream fee
   limits do not constrain a gateway at our pin). A concrete case: zero bases, send
   15_001 ppm, receive 0, low federation fees -- the 200 sats + 3% cap ADMITS that route, but a
   ppm rejection refuses it before sizing, and if it is the only live route the evacuation stays
   pending and the funds stay stranded. An escape hatch must not acquire a second, stricter
   admissibility test that the cap does not need. This restores what the SDK's own fee limits MEANT but do
   not enforce: `send_fee.le(&PaymentFee::SEND_FEE_LIMIT)` (lnv2-client lib.rs:590) compares a
   DERIVED lexicographic `PartialOrd` with `base` as the first field, so `base 99_999 < 100_000`
   makes the whole comparison true and ppm 29_999 sails past the nominal 15_000 limit -- the
   upstream defect this project already reported. Nothing on the gateway side constrains the
   advertised numbers; they are operator parameters.
   Effect on sizing, now that this is a warning rather than a bound: `s_f` is NOT capped, so the
   oscillating band can be made arbitrarily wide by an adversarial gateway. That is accepted --
   the structural-refusal diagnostic in 2c(c) is what makes such a case DIAGNOSABLE, which is the
   property that actually matters. The adversarial fixture in the Tests section remains reachable
   because of the SDK hole; the warning is how an operator learns why. Honest defaults are nowhere near it -- the
   gateway default is 2 sats + 3_000 ppm and the pilot measured ~9 sats on 1_000_000 msat.
2e. `Action::Evacuate` IS SERDE-PERSISTED inside the durable `Intent`
   (`wallet-core/src/types.rs:169`, `:201`), so adding the (base, bps) components per 2b(a)
   changes a live persisted variant. Make them OPTIONAL/defaulted, and define the ABSENT case
   explicitly: a legacy intent carries no components and must retain its STORED absolute
   `fee_cap` rather than retroactively adopting current policy defaults -- an in-flight
   evacuation planned under the old cap must not silently acquire a new one. Add a legacy-intent
   replay test. The scope guard's "only compatibility concession" means the only KIND of
   concession; every live persisted type this bead touches needs it.
3. `Policy` gains the new fields with NAMED default functions --
   `#[serde(default = "default_evac_fee_base_msat")]` and
   `#[serde(default = "default_evac_fee_bps")]` -- so an existing stored policy still decodes AND
   adopts the shipped values. Plain `#[serde(default)]` would be a BUG here: on a numeric field it
   yields ZERO, so a pre-change row would decode to `(0, 0)` -- the pair 3b-bis rejects -- or to a
   zero evacuation cap, under which nothing ever fits and every evacuation livelocks.
   VALIDATE ON THE STANDALONE OVERRIDE PATH TOO, not only at `policy set`: `build_tick_policy`
   (`wallet-cli/src/main.rs:2283-2310`) layers tick/status overrides straight onto `TickPolicy`
   without calling `Policy::validate`, so `--standalone tick --evac-fee-base-msat 0
   --evac-fee-bps 0` would recreate the zero-cap livelock through a door the `policy set` check
   never sees. AC: the standalone override path rejects `(0, 0)` with the same cross-field error. The repo
   already has the correct pattern: `default_max_fee_bps_of_move` (`wallet-api/src/lib.rs:9`,
   used at `:32`). Test a row with BOTH fields absent and assert the shipped values, not that it
   merely decodes. This is NOT a greenfield compatibility shim and must
   not be removed as one: the policy store is LIVE IN PRODUCTION, and the shipped operator
   procedure guarantees that a release adding a policy field lets walletd start on the existing
   row (`docs/real-sats-pilot-runbook.md:321-326`). Dropping it means walletd fails to boot after
   this release.
3b. Adding two `Policy` fields touches more than the allocator. Name and update every propagation
   surface: `wallet-api/src/lib.rs`, `wallet-fedimint/src/tick.rs`,
   `wallet-fedimint/src/service/mod.rs`, both CLI flag sets and their override paths
   (`wallet-cli/src/main.rs`), and `AllocatorSnapshot` (`wallet-core/src/types.rs:80`). Also
   correct `allocator.rs:598-604`, whose diagnostics comments and `max_fee_bps: None` recording
   ("Evacuation sizes off the ABSOLUTE max_fee, not the proportional bps") become false.
3b-bis. VALIDATION BOUNDS for the two new fields, because the degenerate pair silently disables
   evacuation. The existing proportional knob documents and enforces a range and rejects 0
   (`wallet-core/src/types.rs:96-97`). Here: `evac_fee_bps` in `0..=10_000` with 0 ALLOWED (a
   base-only cap is legitimate), `evac_fee_base_msat` unrestricted -- but REJECT THE PAIR
   `(base 0, bps 0)` at `policy set`, since it yields cap 0, nothing ever fits, and the result is
   the indefinite `Retryable` livelock this bead exists to kill, with no refusal at set time.
   Also extend 3b's surface list with the reassembly plumbing 2b(c) forces: `OpArtifact`
   (`move_protocol.rs`) and `op_artifact_from_meta`/backfill (`multi_client.rs:1226-1259`) must
   carry the persisted cap, or the CRASH SAFETY AC cannot pass. State what the corrected
   `allocator.rs:598-604` refusal diagnostics RECORD for the evac components rather than only
   that the old comment is false.
3c. THE LEDGER REPORTS A CAP IT DOES NOT ENFORCE unless this is fixed too. `FeeBreakdown.fee_cap`
   is stamped once from `Intent.max_fee` at plan time (`wallet-core/src/executor.rs:54`,
   `journal.rs:2974-2978`) and `refresh_from_move` copies op-ids, gateway and quoted fees but NOT
   `fee_cap` (`journal.rs:2987-3014`). Plan 75,000 sats -> the row shows a 2,450-sat cap; clamp to
   1,000 sats -> the enforced cap is 230 sats; the row keeps reporting 2,450 for its entire life,
   so a post-incident fee audit against `history` validates fees the enforced cap would have
   refused. Stamp the final recomputed cap onto the ledger row via `refresh_from_move` -- AND the
   final AMOUNT with it. `kind_from_action` seeds the row's amount from the PLANNED action
   (`wallet-core/src/ledger.rs:243`) and `refresh_from_move` copies op-ids, gateway and quotes but
   not `MoveRecord.amount` (`journal.rs:2984`). Refreshing only the cap yields a row reading
   `amount = 75,000 sats, fee_cap = 230 sats` -- internally false, since an auditor recomputing
   from the displayed amount derives 2,450. Refresh BOTH.
   Two more comments go stale and are in scope: `AllocatorSnapshot.max_fee` ("this bounds ONLY
   `Evacuate`", `wallet-core/src/types.rs:92-94`) and the matching `Policy.max_fee` comment
   (`wallet-api/src/lib.rs:20-21`).
4. ADR-0029 is this bead's AUTHORITY: the implementation conforms to it. Only non-semantic
   synchronisation (status line, code references) is in scope here -- a semantic change to the
   cap shape, route ordering or `Move` behaviour requires a separate decision BEFORE
   implementation, never an ADR edit that makes the document match the code. Update
   `README.md` (the policy-knob section) AND
   `docs/real-sats-pilot-runbook.md` §4 so the suggested `policy set` includes the new
   knobs, and state plainly that the absolute `--max-fee` no longer bounds an evacuation.

## Tests

- A full-balance evacuation at the per-federation cap drains in ONE operation at measured rates.
  Do NOT write this as "construct the case that is refused today": at MEASURED rates nothing is
  refused -- the pilot gateway's bases sit far below the 50-sat cap, so it CHUNK-DRAINS (failure
  mode 1 in the problem statement above). The pre-change assertion is therefore that the old code
  sizes down to roughly the 1/27th chunk, not that it refuses. Genuine refusal needs a gateway
  whose SUMMED TWO-LEG QUOTE strictly exceeds the cap (mode 2) -- not merely bases that "meet
  or exceed" it; at exact equality with no other component the quote executes, and it is tested separately in the livelock
  criterion, where refusal IS real. A test that only exercises a small evacuation passes before
  and after and proves nothing.
- A small evacuation (~1,000 sats) whose legitimate fee is a large PERCENTAGE of the amount is
  admitted, proving the base component works. A percentage-only cap must FAIL this test -- try it
  and confirm it goes red, so the test is not vacuous.
- A fee above base + proportional is still REFUSED: the cap must bound a hostile gateway, not
  merely stop refusing.
- Existing `Move` cap behaviour is unchanged, asserted explicitly.
- A stored policy written before this change still decodes and picks up the defaults.

## Scope guard

Do NOT change the per-federation balance cap (ADR-0018 stands), the evacuation trigger, or the
route. Do NOT remove the absolute `max_fee`, but state precisely who keeps it: allocator-generated
funding `Move` stays on the PROPORTIONAL `move_fee_cap(...)` (`allocator.rs:674`, unchanged per
ADR-0029), while the user-facing manual money verbs keep the ABSOLUTE policy default. The earlier
blanket phrasing "`Move` and the manual verbs still use it" contradicted requirement 2 and could
be read as restoring the absolute cap to allocator moves. Do NOT make
evacuation uncapped. Greenfield: the `#[serde(default)]` allowance above is the only compatibility
concession.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CLAMP SAFETY (the 2b criterion; money-critical, currently the easiest hole to ship): a test
      plans an evacuation at a large amount, forces the executor to clamp it to a much smaller net,
      and asserts the permitted fee is base + bps of the EXECUTED amount -- not of the planned one.
      Without this AC an implementation can pass every other criterion here and still authorise a
      75,000-sat-sized cap against a 1,000-sat move.
- [ ] CRASH SAFETY: a killpoint test at `before-move-record` (`executor.rs:1398` -- the receive op
      is committed in the client DB and the `MoveRecord` is not yet persisted) drops the
      `MoveRecord` cache and asserts reassembly restores the final (clamped) cap from `MoveMeta`,
      never the planned-amount cap from `params`.
- [ ] LEDGER AGREEMENT: after a clamp, the ledger row's `fee_cap` equals the ENFORCED cap AND its
      `amount` equals the EXECUTED amount -- asserted after an ordinary clamp and again after
      cache-loss reconstruction. Refreshing only one field leaves the row internally false
      (75,000 sats at a 230-sat cap).
- [ ] POLICY VALIDATION: `policy set` rejects `(base 0, bps 0)` and accepts `bps 0` with a
      non-zero base.
- [ ] ECONOMIC VIABILITY (the b-bis criterion; the largest money-loss hole in this bead): a
      gateway whose best fitting chunk costs MORE than it delivers is refused, not chunk-drained.
      Fixture: cap 200 sats + 3%; gateway SEND base 99 sats and RECEIVE base 49 sats (~148
      combined) and an ASYMMETRIC, SEND-HEAVY ppm split: SEND 940,000 ppm, RECEIVE 10,000 ppm;
      source balance 75,000 sats. PIN BOTH PPMS SEPARATELY, never a combined figure. Gateway fees
      are charged on the GROSS invoice, not the net (`fee.rs:174-181`), so: solvability is governed by
      the RECEIVE ppm ALONE -- `rp >= 1,000,000` leaves nothing deliverable, while a SEND ppm above
      1,000,000 is perfectly solvable and is caught by the viability check instead, so do NOT state
      a COMBINED-ppm threshold (ADR-0029 records this error as already made twice); the receive ppm
      shrinks the contract directly so the hostile load must sit on the SEND leg, and
      a SYMMETRIC split does not reproduce the headline -- at 150,000/150,000 the largest fitting
      chunk nets ~107 sats for a ~65% loss, not ~97%. At 940,000/10,000 the largest cap-fitting
      invoice is ~54.9 sats, delivering ~5.35 sats for a ~200-sat fee against a ~200.16-sat cap,
      giving the ~365 chunks. PRECONDITION, owned here because ADR-0029 delegates the fixture and every
      number in it to this bead: configure federation and mint fees to zero/negligible, or the
      pinned aggregates do not reproduce (a devimint federation's real lnv2 and per-note mint fees
      shift the largest fitting invoice, the per-chunk net and the chunk count). The viability
      CHECK must still include those fees; only the fixture zeroes them. Two earlier revisions charged the ppm against the NET and produced
      fixtures that fail the ORDINARY cap check instead of the viability one -- a false green. DO NOT fixture
      "base just under 200 sats" -- it cannot execute at the pin (see the problem statement) and
      the test would be vacuous.
      Assert the evacuation does NOT proceed over that route, and assert
      red-first that WITHOUT the check it drains ~365 chunks delivering ~1,953 sats while burning
      ~73,047 -- the test must demonstrate the loss it prevents.
- [ ] The efficiency check is a POST-CHECK: assert the sizing search still returns the same `n*`
      as without it (the predicate is unchanged), and that the check is applied to that result.
      A test that folds `fee <= n` into the predicate must FAIL this criterion.
- [ ] NOTE-COUNT DISCONTINUITY: a fixture where `n*` fails the efficiency check by a few msat
      because a note-count boundary raised the fee, while a slightly smaller amount passes, must
      EVACUATE — not refuse. Assert red-first against a top-only implementation.
- [ ] NON-MONOTONE SIZING, INCREASING REGIME: gateway bases EXCEED THE FIXTURE'S CONFIGURED
      20-SAT CAP BASE while ppm is BELOW 300 bps and the evacuation still proceeds. NOTE the bases exceed the CONFIGURED
      20-sat cap base of that fixture, NOT the 200-sat default: 99 + 49 = 148 cannot exceed 200,
      and no executable gateway base can, so stating it against the default makes the criterion
      impossible and leaves the regime untested. Use the 2c worked case (bases 99 + 49,
      ppm 5,000, cap 20 sats + 300 bps, balance 10,000 sats). The LIVELOCK criterion below does
      NOT cover this -- it only requires bases above the OLD 50-sat cap, so a 60-sat-base test
      passes while the hole ships.
- [ ] LIVELOCK / GENUINE REFUSAL: with a gateway whose SUMMED TWO-LEG QUOTE strictly exceeds the
      cap at EVERY amount (fixed component alone above the cap -- e.g. bases 99 + 49 against a
      configured cap base of 100 sats with a 0 bps rate), the evacuation stays `Retryable` AND
      emits 2c(c)'s structural-refusal diagnostic. Red-first: without the diagnostic it retries
      silently forever, which is the failure this bead exists to kill. The Tests section refers
      to this criterion; it must exist.
- [ ] NON-MONOTONE SIZING, DECREASING REGIME (the mirror case): zero-base gateway, combined ppm
      400 bps, balance 75,000 sats. A cap-compliant amount (<= ~20,000 sats) must drain.
- [ ] SIZING NEVER EXCEEDS `desired`: a case where the cap-feasible window starts ABOVE the
      destination's cap room must not size above it. Without the upper bound in 2c(a) the search
      can return ~72,115 sats against 10,000 sats of cap room -- ~62,000 sats over the ADR-0018
      hard cap, with evacuations exempt from the downstream check.
- [ ] STRUCTURAL REFUSAL IS DIAGNOSABLE: on the adversarial knife-edge fixture -- policy
      (base 100_000 msat, bps 300), gateway receive (base 3, ppm 0), send (base 99_999,
      ppm 29_999) -- a refusal MUST carry the structural-refusal diagnostic naming the cap trend;
      a silent indefinite retry fails this criterion.
      Do NOT assert `None` as the required outcome. If the search happens to probe a fitting
      amount, RETURNING IT IS CORRECT: `total_within_cap` compares with `<=` (`fee.rs:160-164`),
      so an exact-cap candidate is admitted and survives an unchanged re-quote, and ADR-0029's
      rule is that only "no amount fits" is a failure. What the robustness contract licenses is
      that the search need not HUNT the oscillating band for such an amount -- not that finding
      one must be discarded. Mandating `None` here would strand an executable evacuation and
      contradict both the exact-cap criterion above and the governing ADR.
- [ ] THE PPM WARNING FIRES, AND DOES NOT GATE: a gateway advertising send ppm 29_999 under a
      sub-limit base produces the warning AND is still admitted if the cap admits it. Assert both
      halves -- the warning present, and the route NOT refused on ppm alone. Today no warning
      exists, because `PaymentFee`'s derived lexicographic ordering compares `base` first and lets
      it past the nominal limit.
- [ ] CAP ARITHMETIC: exact-cap is admitted and cap-plus-one-msat is refused, with the cap derived
      from executed NET and each charged fee derived from its real SDK base.
- [ ] A gateway whose base fees exceed the cap no longer produces an indefinite `Retryable`
      livelock: assert the base+proportional cap admits it, and assert the OLD absolute cap
      refused it (this half IS assertable -- unlike full-size admission, refusal is real here).
- [ ] A full-balance evacuation at the per-federation cap drains the source IN ONE operation.
      State it as: the executed net is the MAXIMAL amount whose net plus BOTH fee legs fits
      spendable. "At full size" is mathematically impossible and must not be written:
      `source_debit = invoice + send_quote` and `invoice = net + receive_quote`
      (`executor.rs:74`, `:91`), so any positive fee makes `source_debit > net` and a 75,000-sat
      balance cannot deliver 75,000 sats net -- at the measured 1.7848% it delivers ~73,685.
      An implementer forcing a literal full-size AC green would omit fees from affordability and
      overdraw. Pin the exact expected net and source debit for the fixture, and assert the OLD
      code returns roughly the 1/27th chunk while the new code returns the one-operation maximum.
- [ ] A small evacuation whose legitimate fee is a large percentage of the amount is admitted, and
      a percentage-only cap is shown to fail that test.
- [ ] A fee exceeding base + proportional is still refused.
- [ ] `Move`'s cap behaviour is unchanged, asserted by test.
- [ ] A pre-existing stored policy decodes and adopts the new defaults.
- [ ] The runbook's suggested policy includes the new knobs and states that `--max-fee` no longer
      bounds an evacuation.

comments.text:
DECOMPOSED 2026-08-07 into three dependent beads. THIS BEAD REMAINS THE CANONICAL SPEC -- the full
derivation, the worked numeric cases, the pinned fixtures and the rejected alternatives all stay here,
and each child points back to it. Do not implement directly against a child without reading this.

  1/3 br-evac-cap-policy-r3n   -- Policy knobs, validation, propagation. Behaviour-neutral.
  2/3 br-evac-cap-enforce-vn6  -- the money change: cap from executed net, persistence, sizing.
  3/3 br-evac-cap-ledger-x9k   -- ledger reports what was enforced; runbook + README.

Why split, and why THIS split: the bead touched wallet-core, wallet-api, wallet-fedimint, wallet-cli,
the journal, the ledger, the move protocol and multi_client in one lock. The seam is DEPLOYABILITY,
not code area -- 1/3 is additive with zero evacuation-behaviour change, 2/3 is the indivisible
invariant (clamp safety + crash safety + sizing are one thing and must not be split further), 3/3 is
reporting that has nothing to report until 2/3 lands. Splitting anywhere inside 2/3 would create an
intermediate state where the cap is computed but not persisted -- the exact crash hazard section 2b
identifies.

This bead closes when all three do; br-recanary-y2j-ujs still hangs off it, so the re-canary fires
against the complete change rather than a third of it.

title: Revert temporary debug RUST_LOG on walletd
description:
## Outcome
walletd runs at its normal log level again.

## Why this exists
`RUST_LOG` was raised to `debug,fm::client::net::api=trace` during the 2026-07-19/20
gateway investigation (issue #8837 / the stuck cross-federation move). That investigation
concluded -- the root cause was `tpe::aggregate_dk_shares` panicking on a single decryption
share and killing the client's `sm-executor`. The verbose level is still on in the
deployment and was never intended to be permanent.

## Scope
Revert the log level in the k3s/ArgoCD deployment (`codeberg.org/zalguod/devops`).

## Critical constraints
Check FIRST whether the refusal-diagnostics work still needs it. Debug logging is currently
the ONLY way an unexplained refusal leaves any trace, since the journal records just
`fed` + `reason`. If `br-ljj.1` has not landed, reverting this removes the only evidence
channel for a failure that is still open and still unreproduced.

## Dependencies / ordering
Prefer to land after `br-ljj.1` (refusal diagnostics persist to the journal), which is what
makes the debug channel redundant.

## Verification
- Acceptance signal: walletd pod logs at normal volume; a subsequent refusal is still
  explainable from its journal row alone.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] walletd pod logs at normal volume.
- [ ] br-ljj.1 has landed first, or a written reason why reverting early is safe.
notes: EXTERNAL/undrainable here (2026-07-23): target repo codeberg.org/zalguod/devops is not checked out in this environment (local devops dirs are dpc/devops, fedibtc/devops-automation, fedibtc/k8s-devops; no walletd RUST_LOG found). Precondition (br-ljj.1 landed) is MET, so it is ready to do wherever that repo lives.
