title: Remove the DAEMON gateway pin; keep standalone --gateway as break-glass
description:
Stop the daemon from pinning a gateway, so automated routing always resolves from the
federation's vetted list. Devimint's daemon-driven smokes register the LDK gateway instead.

Authority: [ADR-0030](docs/adr/0030-automated-routing-is-never-pinned.md).

## What goes and what stays

REMOVED: the `gateway` key in `walletd.toml`, and every path from daemon config to
`FedimintExecutor.pinned_gateway`. After this, the scheduler, allocator, probes and evacuation
can never be pinned.

RETAINED: standalone `wallet-cli --gateway`, as the operator BREAK-GLASS override, ON MONEY VERBS
ONLY. It is REJECTED for `discover`, `probe`, `tick`, `status` and `reconcile`; the AWAIT verbs
keep it, subject to change 3b below
(`wallet-cli/src/main.rs:990`,
`:1067`, `:1142`, `:1174` -- all four build a `Runtime` with the pin today, at `:1012`, `:1098`,
`:1148`, `:1181`). Those verbs run the SAME allocator the daemon runs and write the SAME health
signals it consumes, so a flag reaching them is the daemon pin under another name: a stale
`--gateway` on a standalone `tick` can suppress healthy vetted routes, mark a destination
unusable, and force an evacuation route.

RETAINED, and NOT to be confused with either:
  - `Action::Move { gateway }` / `Action::Evacuate { gateway }` -- a route HINT, re-resolved
    under the same cap when it no longer holds (`wallet-core/src/types.rs:187-196`, checked at
    `executor.rs:306-319`). NOTE the check today validates ENDPOINTS ONLY and does not re-test
    vetted-list membership, so do not read "still serves" here as though the membership half
    holds; `CONTEXT.md`'s Route hint entry carries the caveat, and br-s0e owns closing it.
  - `Action::Pay { gateway }` / `Action::Receive { gateway }` -- a `Some` becomes a singleton
    candidate set with no registered-list fallback (`executor.rs:1017-1027`, `:1133-1138`). Do NOT
    describe these as the durable form of the break-glass: the flag does not populate them. Every
    production constructor passes `gateway: None` (`wallet-cli/src/main.rs:1460`, `:1545`;
    `wallet-daemon/src/handlers.rs:313`, `:382`), and the only setter has no production callers.
    The flag reaches money verbs through the executor fallback
    `gateway.clone().or_else(|| self.pinned_gateway.clone())` (`executor.rs:1024`, `:1135`), which
    is DELIBERATELY non-durable -- (SCOPED, per ADR-0030: non-durability governs route SELECTION only --
   once an operation has committed the PERSISTED ROUTE is authoritative and replays without the
   flag. RELEASE WINDOW, stated rather than inherited: this bead lands BEFORE br-s0e, and today's
   backfill retains neither the source gateway nor the route kind, so until br-s0e adds route
   persistence a committed break-glass `Move` that crashes before its `MoveRecord` is written has
   NO recorded route to replay -- it re-resolves from the vetted list or stalls. Accepted for that
   window; do not write an AC asserting authoritative replay before br-s0e lands. Unqualified, this permits post-commit re-resolution, which can re-resolve under a
   committed invoice or stall because the unvetted gateway is on no list.)
   "The pin is deliberately NOT journaled into the intent, so a pin
    change applies to re-drives after a restart" (`executor.rs:1019-1021`). Consequences for the
    implementer: that `.or_else` fallback is NOT dead code and must not be removed, and the flag
    must NOT be journaled into intents to make a durability story true.

## Why

The break-glass and the daemon pin were ONE field with two meanings, and the codebase asserted
both:
- `wallet-daemon/src/config.rs:36-37`: "Host config -- which gateway is reachable is a DEPLOYMENT
  FACT, NOT USER POLICY."
- `wallet-fedimint/src/executor.rs:279`: "An OPERATOR PIN overrides route selection entirely,
  planning included."
`resolve_move_gateway` implements the second in its strongest form: it returns the pin
UNCONDITIONALLY, without checking that it serves the route (`executor.rs:303-305`). Splitting the
concept resolves the contradiction; ADR-0030 records which half survives where.

The daemon pin also reaches beyond route selection. A pinned daemon hands the pin to every
federation probe, which then validates only that gateway and never scans the registered list
(`probe.rs:458`); the resulting `probed_ok: false` mapping (`probe.rs:170`) makes the allocator drop that
federation as an evacuation destination (`allocator.rs:444` -- `receive_blocker`'s `probed_ok` gate -- and `:475`,
   `eligible_for_evacuation`). A standing config could
therefore disable evacuation entirely while executor-level tests stayed green.

Nothing deployed relies on it, VERIFIED rather than inferred: the live `walletd.toml` is a
ConfigMap carrying exactly `data_dir`, `address`, `port`, `token_path`, `log_level`
(`/home/master/newmachine/remote-devops/k8s/argo/walletd/walletd.yaml:24-29`), launched with only
`--config` (`:82`). Production has always run unpinned, so nothing deployed relies
on the pin today. Do NOT extend that into "the vetted lists are all fine": a production pay runs
with `gateway: None` (`wallet-daemon/src/handlers.rs:313`) and scans only the SOURCE federation's
list (`executor.rs:1024-1027`), so the 2026-07-28 canary proves ONE federation's list serves, not
every joined federation's. That gap is exactly what the PRE-FLIGHT acceptance criterion checks
before any code is removed.

Why the break-glass survives: explicit-gateway `send`/`receive` skip the vetted list and check
only `routing_info` (`fedimint-lnv2-client/src/lib.rs:574-587`), so the flag is the only way this
wallet reaches an unvetted gateway. The runbook's gateway-outage remedy -- "moving funds is a
manual operation" (`docs/real-sats-pilot-runbook.md:290-295`) -- silently depends on it: with a
dead or empty vetted list, a manual verb WITHOUT `--gateway` fails exactly as automation does.
The incident is a live-but-unadministered federation whose vetted gateways are all dead:
consensus still redeems, only a guardian can `gateways add`, and the operator would otherwise
need a code release.

## Relationship to br-s0e

Registration (required change 1) is br-s0e's real prerequisite -- devimint's EMPTY VETTED LIST is
what blocks its gate, not the pin. A gate smoke that registers gateways and passes no `--gateway`
exercises the existing no-pin fallback (`executor.rs:344-349`) today.

What THIS bead buys br-s0e is that its four-case pin table becomes unreachable rather than
merely unspecified. br-s0e has already been amended accordingly; do not re-add it.

If this bead stalls on the responsiveness rework, required change 1 (registration) can land alone
and unblock br-s0e's LIVE-GATE PREREQUISITE -- but ONLY that. br-s0e also depends on automated
routing becoming unpinnable, which needs the rest of this bead; registration alone does not make
the pin cases unreachable.

## Required changes

1. DAEMON-DRIVEN SMOKES REGISTER THE GATEWAY as a setup step -- ON EVERY GUARDIAN, FOR EVERY
   FEDERATION. Vetting is a per-peer DB write behind `check_auth`, not a consensus item
   (`fedimint-lnv2-server/src/lib.rs:696-704`, `:890-898`), and `request_admin` targets a SINGLE
   peer (`fedimint-api-client/src/api/mod.rs:372-391`). The client's `gateways()` union returns at
   the first n-f valid responses (`FilterMapThreshold`, `fedimint-api-client/src/query.rs:78`,
   `:89`), so a gateway vetted on 1 of 4 guardians is visible only when that guardian is among the
   first three to answer -- nondeterministic flakiness, not a clean failure.
   REGISTER ON ALL REACHABLE GUARDIANS, not a computed minimum -- and note that the registration
   count and any SUPPORT gate are DIFFERENT thresholds: registering on exactly `2f+1` does not
   guarantee `2f+1` supporting responses, since a Byzantine registered peer can answer empty.
   `br-gw-threshold-membership-k4t` owns reconciling them. `f+1` is NOT enough under the Byzantine
   model this project assumes. The intersection argument only puts a registered peer in the quorum, not one that ANSWERS
   TRUTHFULLY: with `n=4, f=1`, registering on {A, B} where A is Byzantine admits the quorum
   {A, C, D}, where A returns empty and C, D were never registered, so the union loses the URL. At
   `2f+1` every `n-f` quorum holds at least `f+1` registered peers, so at least one honest
   registered peer answers. (`f+1` is sufficient for CRASH faults only.) Requiring EVERY guardian
   would make repair impossible while one is unavailable, which is the incident this serves:
   register on all REACHABLE guardians, gate on `2f+1`.
   Upstream's own template at our pinned rev loops gateways x peers:
     `fedimint-cli --our-id <peer> --password <pw> module lnv2 gateways add <url>`
   (`fedimint-lnv2-tests/bin/tests.rs:150-157`, `:581-598`). NOTE devimint's comment calling this
   "an explicit consensus item" (`devimint/src/federation.rs:1170-1172`) is STALE.
   `update_gateway_map` is NOT needed: the wallet enumerates live via `list_gateways(None)`
   (`multi_client.rs:755-763`) and always passes the gateway explicitly. Two-fed smokes need a
   client joined to fed B to run B's add-loop.
2. DROP `gateway` FROM `walletd.toml` (`wallet-daemon/src/config.rs`, `wallet-daemon/src/main.rs`
   -- the plumbing at `main.rs:247-274` goes). Also delete wallet-cli's `_gateway` field
   (`wallet-cli/src/main.rs:861-865`), which tolerates the key so standalone can read `data_dir`
   from a daemon config: once walletd rejects that file, standalone must not silently accept it.
   A `pinned_gateway` grep will not catch it -- it is named `_gateway`.
3a. ENFORCE THE NO-PIN RULE AT THE RUNTIME BOUNDARY, not only at the CLI. Telling the CLI to
   pass `None` closes the operator-facing door; it does not close the door. An in-process caller
   can still construct `Runtime::new(.., Some(gateway), ..)` and invoke the public `tick`, the
   public `reconcile()`, OR the public `active_probe` (`runtime.rs:1758`, whose money legs reach
   `do_move` on an executor built from `self.pinned_gateway` -- `runtime.rs:593`, `:2190-2196`).
   Those three are automated entry points, AND THE ENUMERATION IS NOT THE FIX -- ADR-0030 records
   that counting them failed three times and is STILL short: `Runtime::watch_once`
   (`runtime.rs:1088`) is public and composes all three plus the discover pass, and
   `FedimintExecutor` is publicly re-exported (`wallet-fedimint/src/lib.rs:56`) with a public
   constructor that takes the override (`executor.rs:176`), so `Executor::perform` can be handed
   an allocator-created `Move`/`Evacuate` past every `Runtime` method.
   REQUIRED: automated routing must never observe the override, proven at the API level rather
   than the CLI. `ReasonCode` is caller-supplied, so it dispatches -- it does not authorise; the
   entitlement has to come from the construction path. WHICH STRUCTURAL SHAPE ships (a distinct money-only
   type, or construction-path separation) is the implementer's call: the acceptance test is what
   binds. Clearing the override at each automated entry point is NOT a shippable shape --
   `watch_once` composes them and `FedimintExecutor` is publicly constructible, so the
   executor-boundary criterion stays red by construction. Interim during development only. Gate by ACTION PROVENANCE at the EXECUTOR boundary -- the one place every route
   resolution funnels through -- so the override is reachable only on a money-only path. Rejecting
   or clearing per method is acceptable ONLY as an interim, with a direct test per method, and it
   carries the standing risk that the next public composition reopens the hole. The test that
   proves the structural version is a direct `Executor::perform` call with an allocator-created
   action under an active override.
   The three are named below as symptoms, and `reconcile` is the worse of the
   two because it re-drives every pending intent, so an override reaching it pins allocator-made
   `Move` and `Evacuate` alike. Rejecting the CLI flag does not close the API path for either.
   `Runtime` hands that override to `FedimintExecutor`, whose `resolve_move_gateway` uses it
   unconditionally -- so automated execution stays pinnable while every other criterion in this
   bead passes. These are NOT coequal options: the break-glass moves to a money-only
   path the automated callers cannot carry, gated by action provenance at the executor boundary.
   Per-method reject/clear is the INTERIM only. Either way it needs a DIRECT API-level test; a
   CLI test cannot observe this. ADR-0030 states the rule independently
   of process, which is why CLI-level enforcement is not enough.
3b. SCOPE `await_standalone`'S RECOVERY TO THE REQUESTED KEY. It currently calls
   `client.reconcile()` unconditionally as its first step (`wallet-cli/src/main.rs:1719`), a full
   re-drive of EVERY pending intent -- so `--gateway <url> await-move <key>` pins the re-drive of
   every pending allocator move and evacuation, the same hazard `reconcile` is rejected for.
   Do NOT fix this by rejecting the flag on await: that would stop an operator awaiting the very
   payment they just made with the break-glass, and 13 of the 15 smokes call an await verb through
   a `--gateway` helper. Drive only the awaited key instead. Keep the off-actor ledger repair that
   follows it -- that is not a re-drive.
   SCOPING ALONE IS NOT SUFFICIENT: if the requested key names a scheduler- or allocator-created
   `Move`/`Evacuate`, driving just that key still routes an AUTOMATED intent under the override.
   Scoping only protects the OTHER pending intents. So gate the override on the target intent's
   PROVENANCE, -- ENTITLEMENT comes from the durable authenticated
   origin marker below; `ReasonCode` is caller-supplied and may only DISPATCH an already-authorised
   override, never authorise one. Read the leg's `ReasonCode` for dispatch, not `Actor`: a manual probe calls
   `active_probe(.., Actor::User)` (`wallet-cli/src/main.rs:1106`) but stamps its legs
   `ReasonCode::ActiveProbe` (`wallet-fedimint/src/runtime.rs:2234`), so an actor check reads
   "user" for a probe-lane leg and reopens the backdoor. Test with a manual probe-leg key.
   THREE outcomes, matching ADR-0030 exactly: user-initiated AND route-resolving -> APPLY;
   user-initiated but resolving no route (a `Join`, `runtime.rs:1025-1030`) -> APPLY AND NO-OP,
   never refuse -- `smoke_money`'s `join_fed` awaits a join key through a `--gateway` helper
   (`smoke_money_devimint.sh:74`, `:77-79`) and refusing breaks a smoke this bead promises to
   leave untouched; automated reason code -> REFUSE. Refusal is for automated provenance only.
   Refuse it with a clear
   message (not a silent drop) when awaiting an automated one. REFUSING is the disposition, not
   ignoring -- ADR-0030's own Rejected-vs-Ignored taxonomy makes that distinction load-bearing,
   so do not read its "must not carry" as licensing a silent drop.
   AC: `--gateway <url> await-move <allocator-created-key>` does NOT reach route resolution with
   the pin set.
3. STANDALONE PASSES `None` FOR THE AUTOMATED VERBS. `pinned_gateway` STAYS in `executor.rs` and
   `runtime.rs` -- that is how the break-glass reaches route resolution on money verbs.
   DELETE the pinned branches at `probe.rs:463`, `route_econ.rs:301` AND `runtime.rs:3127`
   (`route_gateway_candidates`, reached only from `validate_executor_move_route` at
   `runtime.rs:3076` -- the tick/status planning preflight). Keeping the FIELD in `runtime.rs` so
   the break-glass reaches the executor is separable from keeping that pinned BRANCH, which is
   unreachable for exactly the same reason as the other two. Probes and route
   economics run only under `discover`/`probe`/`tick`/`status`, exactly the verbs this bead makes
   reject the flag, and the daemon can no longer set the pin -- so after this bead those branches
   are unreachable from every caller. Leaving them is dead code that reads like a supported path,
   and an implementer following the old blanket "it stays in these four files" rationale would
   keep them without noticing the justification no longer applies there. What changes: the daemon can no longer set it, and
   `discover`/`probe`/`tick`/`status`/`reconcile` REJECT the flag rather than silently ignoring
   it. `reconcile` is the one most easily missed and the worst to miss: it re-drives EVERY pending
   intent (`main.rs:681`, `:1590`), allocator-created moves and evacuations included, so a flag on
   it pins automated money operations wholesale. (An
   operator who passed it deserves to know it does not apply).
   Do NOT make `resolve_move_gateway`'s pinned branch conditional. Per ADR-0030 the break-glass
   deliberately skips the PRESELECTION validation -- vetted-list membership and the two-end
   `serves` precheck -- but NOT the operation's own `routing_info` liveness check, which still
   applies. Do not restate this as "does not validate" flat. An operator routing around a dead
   vetted list is overriding the PRESELECTION on purpose, and `gateway_serves_route` would validate BOTH ends through the gateway
   (`executor.rs:459-469`), and running it would re-impose the membership test the flag exists to
   step around. It is NOT a licence to reach a one-end-only gateway: the operation's own liveness
   checks refuse one before anything is minted, and they stay.
4. CORRECT THE TWO CONTRADICTING DOC COMMENTS. `config.rs:36-37` goes with the field.
   `executor.rs:279` must be REWRITTEN, not deleted -- the branch survives -- to describe a
   money-verb break-glass rather than "an operator pin [that] overrides route selection entirely,
   planning included". The `--gateway` doc comment (`wallet-cli/src/main.rs:71-72`) currently
   advertises "EVERY route this invocation resolves (money verbs, probes, ticks)" and must be
   narrowed to the four money verbs PLUS the provenance-eligible await verbs
   (`await-receive`, `await-send`, `await-move`) -- "money verbs" is the ADR's shorthand, not
   exact CLI documentation.
5. DOCUMENTATION, precisely:
   - `README.md:124` ("gateway pinning details") -- update to the split.
   - `docs/archive/route-economics-decisions.md` Q4 records the OPPOSITE as a standing decision
     ("`pinned_gateway` overrides route-economics selection entirely"), and it is the very branch
     change 3 deletes. A superseded-by-ADR-0030 banner has been added; verify it is still accurate
     when this lands, so an implementer sent to delete `route_econ.rs:301` does not find a
     "settled questions" document defending it.
   - `CONTEXT.md` already carries "Break-glass gateway override" and "Vetted list"; keep them
     consistent with whatever ships. "Route hint" also survives.
   - `docs/devimint-runbook.md` -- update the empty-vetted-list gotcha to describe registration.
     Do NOT delete its `--gateway` documentation: that is `fedimint-cli`'s OWN flag on
     `module lnv2 send`, untouched by this bead.
   - Runtime diagnostics recommending `--gateway` (`executor.rs:350-355`, `tick.rs:379-382`) must
     distinguish: for a daemon-driven failure the remedy is guardian-side `gateways add`; for
     standalone money verbs the break-glass stands.
   - The runbook's gateway-outage entry must DOCUMENT the break-glass explicitly instead of
     leaving "moving funds is a manual operation" to imply it: name `--gateway`, say it bypasses

## Which smokes change -- THIRTEEN of fifteen, re-measured

TWO separate reasons force conversion, and an earlier draft of this bead counted only the first,
claiming "only 5 need conversion, 9 need none". That was wrong; these numbers are measured.

Reason 1 -- they set the DAEMON pin (`gateway = ` in walletd.toml), which is being removed:
  smoke_daemon, smoke_soak, smoke_responsiveness, smoke_recover, smoke_daemon_chain.

Reason 2 -- their `wcli`/`wsa` helper appends `--gateway` to EVERY invocation, and they invoke
verbs that change 3 makes REJECT the flag. A rejecting verb plus a global helper flag is a hard
failure, not a no-op:
  smoke_probe    -- `wcli status` (`:136`)
  smoke_tick     -- `wcli tick` (`:189`, `:246`)
  smoke_discover -- `wcli discover` (`:99`)
  smoke_evacuate -- `wcli status` (`:212`), `wcli tick` (`:234`)
  smoke_history  -- rejecting-verb calls via the helper

ALSO reason 2, found only after `reconcile` joined the rejection list: smoke_crash_move
(`:227`, `:269`), smoke_directinflow (`:168`) and smoke_move (`:237`) each call `wcli reconcile`
through the same `--gateway` helper.

Genuinely unaffected, TWO: `smoke_money` and `smoke_devimint.sh`.

THIS COUNT HAS BEEN WRONG FIVE TIMES -- "five of fourteen", "ten of fifteen", once more in the
acceptance criterion after the body had been corrected, "14 of the 15" carried into ADR-0030 and
back into this bead, and finally the reason-1/reason-2 OVERLAP: smoke_daemon_chain (`:99`),
smoke_soak (`:105`) and smoke_responsiveness (`:109`) each call `wsa discover` through a
`--gateway` helper AS WELL AS setting the daemon pin, so three of the five "pin" smokes need BOTH
fixes and only smoke_daemon and smoke_recover are pin-only. Each miss came from restating the
split without re-measuring it. RE-MEASURE IT whenever that list
changes. The bead's own instruction to grep each script was not applied to the bead's own list,
which is the exact mistake this paragraph exists to warn about.

The lesson for the implementer: a global `--gateway` on a helper function means you cannot judge
a smoke by which pin it sets. Grep each script for the verbs in change 3 before assuming it is
unaffected.

## smoke_responsiveness is different in kind

It does not pin the LDK gateway; it pins a deliberately NEVER-RESPONDING double
(`smoke_responsiveness_devimint.sh:90` writes `gateway = "http://127.0.0.1:$DOUBLE_PORT/"` into
walletd.toml; standalone seeding uses `--gateway "$GW_REAL"` at `:94`). The gate works BECAUSE
the daemon pin returns with no serves-check, driving money ops into the hang -- the ADR-0024 /
§6a.9 accepts-then-never-settles condition. Once the daemon cannot pin, the double must be
reachable through the vetted list instead, and a never-responding double can never pass
`validate_gateway` (`multi_client.rs:958-964`).

REQUIRED, as budgeted scope: rework `hang_gateway.py` into a REQUEST-LEVEL HTTP double -- not the
accept-level TCP logger it is today (`hang_gateway.py:43-47`). It answers `routing_info` with
valid per-federation data (so it validates, registers and is selectable) and parks ONLY the
invoice/payment endpoints.
Request-level is mandatory, not a refinement: the timing oracle assumes the next accepted TCP
connection belongs to the just-submitted pay (`:168-189`), but HTTP connections are pooled and
reused at our pinned rev (`fedimint-connectors/src/http.rs:57-61`) and an explicit send performs a
`routing_info` request first (`fedimint-lnv2-client/src/lib.rs:574-586`). Once `routing_info`
answers, one driver makes several requests and later drivers reuse a connection: M1/M2/M3 can
attribute an earlier driver's request to the new pay, or see no new accept at all. The gate then
false-greens, false-reds, or stops measuring "POST -> first external call".
So: log endpoint, timestamp and correlation data PER REQUEST; ensure each earlier driver reaches
its parked endpoint before the next measurement; DEMONSTRATE the revised oracle goes red under an
injected delay.
Sequence the registry changes: vet the real gateway on EVERY guardian -> seed -> `gateways remove`
the real gateway on EVERY guardian -> vet the double. `REMOVE_GATEWAY_ENDPOINT` is the same
per-peer `check_auth` write as add (`fedimint-lnv2-server/src/lib.rs:707-716`), so a single-peer
removal leaves the real gateway threshold-nondeterministically visible.
Preserve every double-log, latency, admission-cap, deliberate-red and shutdown assertion. This is
the suite's ONLY live responsiveness/admission/shutdown gate.

## Sequencing -- do not delete first

If `gateways add` does not work against a devimint federation, every converted smoke breaks at
once. So:
  a. Prove registration works in ONE smoke with the daemon pin still set. NOTE the limit: every
     resolution path short-circuits on the pin (`executor.rs:303`, `:341`; `probe.rs:463`;
     `runtime.rs:3127`; `route_econ.rs:301`), so this proves only that `gateways add` returned
     true -- not that resolution uses the list. Step (b) is the real proof.
  b. Confirm green with the daemon pin REMOVED and registration in place, on one SINGLE-FED and
     one TWO-FED smoke (two-fed needs the harness patch and an add-loop against fed B).
  c. Convert `smoke_responsiveness` separately, with its own proof.
  d. Convert any remaining affected smokes and prove them green in ONE landing; DELETE the daemon
     plumbing in a SECOND. Combining them makes a smoke-specific failure bisect to the deletion.
Conversion is worth doing for its own sake: today NO smoke exercises the registered-scan path,
because every one of them pins -- the code production actually runs has zero live coverage.

## Scope guard

Do NOT add a new override knob, and do not widen the surviving flag: it is a break-glass, not
configuration. Do NOT reintroduce a daemon-side pin under another name. Do NOT change route
resolution semantics beyond removing the daemon's ability to set a pin. The route HINT's SHAPE
stays as it is -- but that must NOT be read as freezing the hint's membership check, which br-s0e
is required to tighten. If automated counterparty control is
ever genuinely wanted, that is a new decision with its own ADR.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] PRE-FLIGHT, before any code is removed: `gateways list` is non-empty and validating for
      EVERY joined production federation. The deployed config is already confirmed pin-free; this
      checks the other half -- that nothing depends on the fallback being there.
- [ ] Registration is performed on EVERY guardian of EVERY federation, and BOTH the per-peer
      lists and the aggregate list are asserted. A single-guardian registration that happens to
      pass is the flake this AC exists to prevent.
- [ ] One SINGLE-FED and one TWO-FED smoke each register and pass with the daemon pin REMOVED,
      run and green, before any other smoke is converted.
- [ ] `smoke_responsiveness` passes with the reworked request-level double, retaining its hang,
      latency, admission-cap, deliberate-red and shutdown assertions, and its revised timing
      oracle is shown to go red under an injected delay.
- [ ] Every devimint smoke passes, each RUN not merely edited -- the THIRTEEN converted and the
      TWO unaffected (`smoke_money`, `smoke_devimint.sh`). This count has now gone stale FIVE
      times; take it from the measured split above, and re-measure if the rejection list changes
      again. Note three of the five "pin" smokes ALSO need their helper fixed.
- [ ] `wallet-daemon` cannot set a pin: no `gateway` key, and no path from daemon config to
      `pinned_gateway`. NOT "the symbol appears nowhere" -- it survives on the standalone path.
- [ ] BREAK-GLASS VIABILITY, SCOPED TO THE PRE-COMMIT QUOTE: an explicitly-`--gateway` money
      operation whose QUOTED total fee exceeds what it delivers is REFUSED before committing. It
      cannot bind after commit -- an unvetted gateway can change `routing_info` between the
      executor's quote and the SDK's send-time fetch, there is no local cap re-check there, and
      the SDK's lexicographic limit admits the higher ppm. Test the pre-commit refusal and record
      the post-commit race as the residual it is. The cap alone does not catch this (a named
      gateway can charge more than the net and still sit under the default cap), and br-y2j's
      post-check is scoped to evacuation sizing. ADR-0030 assigns this here.
- [ ] IGNORED BUCKET: `--gateway` on a no-route verb (`join`, `balance`, `history`, `show`,
      `list-feds`, `policy`, `health`, `candidates`, `approve`, `recover`) exits ZERO and behaves
      identically to the flagless invocation. ADR-0030 makes Ignored a load-bearing third bucket
      and `smoke_money` depends on it (`join` at `:77`, `balance` at `:85`). Without this an
      implementation that REJECTS the flag on every non-money, non-await verb passes every other
      criterion while diverging from the taxonomy.
- [ ] DURABLE ORIGIN FOR AWAIT RE-DRIVES: persist an AUTHENTICATED origin marker when a money
      verb creates the intent, and gate the re-drive on it. The marker is OPTIONAL with a
      named default (absent = NOT operator-originated), and BOUND TO THE INTENT it
      authorises (idempotency key + action) so it cannot be lifted onto a cloned intent: existing persisted `Intent` rows carry
      only `Action`/`ReasonCode`, so a required field would make pre-upgrade pending rows fail to
      decode and be skipped by reconcile. This is the ONLY exit -- "narrow
      acceptance so await never carries the override" contradicts this bead's own criteria (every
      await verb must still ACCEPT the flag) and ADR-0030's settled rule, which `smoke_money`
      depends on. A
      capability alone proves only that the CURRENT invocation used an operator path; the target
      intent persists only publicly constructible `Action`/`ReasonCode` and the override is
      non-durable, so on a later `--gateway await-*` a forged `UserInitiated` allocator move is
      indistinguishable from the manual move being legitimately re-driven. ADR-0030 states the
      same; the criterion below cannot be met without this.
- [ ] ACTION-CARRIED GATEWAY: an in-process caller constructing `Action::Pay`/`Action::Receive`
      with `gateway: Some(..)` does NOT obtain an unvetted route. `drive_intent_step` PREFERS that
      value over `pinned_gateway` (`executor.rs:1024`, `:1135`), so removing the executor field
      alone leaves this door open; "the only setter has no production callers" is not the
      structural guarantee. ADR-0030 names this as the second door.
- [ ] FORGED PROVENANCE: an allocator-shaped `Move`/`Evacuate` STAMPED `ReasonCode::UserInitiated`
      by an in-process caller does NOT obtain a pinned route. This is the criterion that separates
      a structural gate from a reason-code one: the executor-boundary test below uses an
      allocator-stamped action, which a caller-supplied reason check would refuse and thereby
      pass, so without this case that gate looks compliant while remaining forgeable.
- [ ] EXECUTOR BOUNDARY (the criterion that actually closes this): a direct
      `FedimintExecutor::perform` call with an ALLOCATOR-created `Move`/`Evacuate` under an active
      override does NOT pin route resolution -- constructed straight from the public re-export
      (`lib.rs:56`, `executor.rs:176`), bypassing every `Runtime` method. Passing the three
      per-method criteria below while failing this one means the bead shipped the enumeration
      ADR-0030 rejects. `Runtime::watch_once` (`runtime.rs:1088`) is covered transitively by
      whatever satisfies this.
- [ ] API BOUNDARY: constructing `Runtime::new(.., Some(gateway), ..)` and calling `tick` does
      NOT pin automated routing -- asserted by a direct API test, not through the CLI.
- [ ] API BOUNDARY, THIRD ENTRY POINT: the same construction followed by `active_probe` does NOT
      pin either leg's routing, asserted by its own direct API test. The daemon-driven probe test
      uses an UNPINNED runtime and cannot detect this, and §3b's manual-probe test covers the
      await backdoor, which is a different hole. Do NOT read this as "three is the complete set"
      -- ADR-0030 records that count as its own error.
- [ ] API BOUNDARY, SECOND ENTRY POINT: the same construction followed by `reconcile()` does NOT
      pin automated routing either, asserted by its own direct API test. `reconcile` is the worse
      of the two -- it re-drives EVERY pending intent -- and a `tick`-only test passes green while
      `reconcile()` still forwards the override. If the implementation instead separates the
      override structurally so neither API can receive it, that discharges both criteria; say so
      in the PR rather than leaving one untested.
- [ ] A daemon-driven evacuation, move, probe and tick each resolve from the vetted list, proven
      by test -- the paths that previously short-circuited on the pin.
- [ ] `wallet-cli --standalone --gateway <url> tick` (and `probe`, `discover`, `status`) is
      REJECTED with a non-zero exit naming the verb -- INCLUDING `reconcile` -- asserted
      red-first: today all of them accept it. Separately assert that EACH of the three await verbs (`await-receive`, `await-send`, `await-move`) still ACCEPTS
      and hand it to `Runtime`.
- [ ] A standalone MONEY verb with `--gateway` still routes through an UNVETTED gateway. This is
      the positive case; without it an over-zealous reading of the rejection AC deletes the
      capability ADR-0030 exists to preserve.
- [ ] `resolve_move_gateway`'s pinned branch is UNCHANGED and still returns without a
      serves-check, reachable only from standalone money verbs and the provenance-eligible
   await verbs (`await-receive`, `await-send`, `await-move`) -- this bead separately requires
   those to accept the override, so "money verbs" alone is a stale twin. Asserted by test that with no pin
      set every resolution validates, and that the break-glass path does not.
- [ ] A `walletd.toml` carrying a `gateway` key is REJECTED, and so is a standalone invocation
      reading that same file -- both asserted by process-level tests with non-zero exits. Do NOT
      build a bespoke pre-parse detector: both structs already carry
      `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` (`wallet-daemon/src/config.rs:46`, test at `:435-442`;
      `wallet-cli/src/main.rs:849-866`), so deleting the fields makes rejection automatic with
      "unknown field `gateway`". A hand-rolled detector is a compatibility shim by another name.
- [ ] The combined pin/hint test (`executor.rs:2629-2671`) is SPLIT, not deleted: the
      daemon-pin-wins half goes, the dead-hint-falls-back-to-registered half REMAINS.

title: Gateway list: threshold-supported membership + bounded ingestion
description:
Close two gaps ADR-0030 names as residuals and both routing beads deliberately exclude.

Authority: [ADR-0030](docs/adr/0030-automated-routing-is-never-pinned.md) -- the union bullet and
the ingestion note.

1. THRESHOLD-SUPPORTED MEMBERSHIP. `gateways()` returns a UNION: `FilterMapThreshold` thresholds
   the RESPONSE COUNT, then every URL any responding guardian returned is flattened into one set
   (`fedimint-lnv2-client/src/api.rs:84-116`). So a single guardian -- Byzantine, compromised or
   merely misconfigured -- can place a gateway in the automated candidate set that no threshold
   ever admitted. "On the vetted list" is therefore NOT a threshold property today, and ADR-0030
   says so explicitly rather than assuming it away.
   REQUIRED: query per peer and require `2f+1` supporting responses before a URL is admitted to
   the automated candidate set. Note the SDK's breadth-of-vetting sort is only a preference and
   does not survive br-s0e's largest-sized-net selection, which has no support term -- so this is
   the real fix, and br-s0e landing makes it MORE urgent, not less.

2. BOUNDED INGESTION, PER PEER RESPONSE. `gateways()` materialises the complete union and then
   computes support with `response.contains` for every entry against every peer response --
   quadratic in one large injected vector -- BEFORE any wallet-side scan bound can apply. A
   per-peer response/body limit (discard the offending peer's response, journal which peer) or a
   bounded per-peer query path is required; capping the AGGREGATE is both too late and wrong,
   since truncating the union discards honest gateways.
   Deliberately kept OUT of the evacuation beads: a guardian set on stalling a client has cheaper
   levers those beads correctly do not defend against, and generic response hardening is
   client-wide, not evacuation spec.

## Rollout
Enforcing the support gate can REMOVE a currently-working production gateway from every automated
candidate set the moment it ships, if fewer than `2f+1` guardians presently return it -- a state
today's union API explicitly permits. So: measure per-guardian support for every gateway the
production federations actually use BEFORE enforcing, and register BEYOND it: writes are not supporters, since a Byzantine peer can
acknowledge the write and still return an empty list, so registering exactly `2f+1` can yield only
`2f` supporters. Register on every reachable guardian and verify OBSERVED support meets the gate
before enabling it.
Ship the measurement and the registration, then the gate.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A URL returned by fewer than `2f+1` peers is NOT admitted to the automated candidate set.
- [ ] An operator break-glass gateway is unaffected -- it never consults the list.
- [ ] A single peer returning an oversized vector does not cause unbounded allocation or
      quadratic work; the offending response is discarded and journalled with its peer id.
- [ ] The existing routing smokes still pass with registration at `2f+1`.

title: Phase 7: encrypt the seed at rest (passphrase-derived key, crash-safe migration)
description:
Encrypt the daemon's seed at rest. ADR-0026 is ACCEPTED but explicitly deferred the build and
said "a follow-up implementation bead carries the ratified choice" — that bead was never filed.
This is it.

Today `load_or_generate_mnemonic` -> `store_encodable_client_secret` writes PLAINTEXT entropy
(wallet-daemon/src/main.rs). Anyone who can read the data directory owns every sat. The only
mitigations in force are host FDE, single-user isolation, and the runbook's ~150k ceiling — none
of which are app-level, and all of which the runbook itself calls interim.

RATIFY ADR-0026's recommendation: operator passphrase-derived key (option 1), Argon2id KDF +
XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD over the stored entropy. Adopt option 2 (KMS/HSM) only if that infra
already exists; do not add it for the pilot.

Required:
1. The passphrase must NOT come from a plaintext k8s Secret or a bare env var. Source it from an
   external secret manager or an interactive unseal. A restart that silently re-reads a plaintext
   secret from the same host defeats the entire control — ADR-0026 says so in as many words.
   Whatever is chosen, DOCUMENT the honest boundary: the seed's protection reduces to the
   protection of the passphrase source.
2. FAIL CLOSED when the passphrase/key source is unavailable at start. Never fall back to
   plaintext, and never generate a fresh seed because the old one would not decrypt — that is
   silent fund loss wearing the costume of a clean first run.
3. One-time re-encrypt of the EXISTING plaintext store on upgrade. Greenfield, so this is a
   migration step, not a serde compat layer. It must be crash-safe: a power loss mid-migration
   must leave either the old plaintext store or the new encrypted one intact and loadable, never
   a half-written store. Prove it with an injected-failure test at each step, not by inspection.
4. `walletd mnemonic` export and `restore-mnemonic` keep working (decrypt on demand).
5. Recovery of PENDING operations — not just ecash — must keep working under encryption.
   ADR-0026's Consequences names this explicitly.
6. Define and test the crash-restart path. The daemon is 24/7 and restarts unattended; if unseal
   is interactive, an unattended restart is a hard outage, and that trade-off must be a stated,
   documented decision rather than a surprise at 3am.

Blocking relationship: this is the stated precondition in ADR-0028's Consequences for exposing
`wallet-web` beyond loopback. It does not block the 6c build, but wallet-web must NOT be
documented for proxy/overlay/public exposure until this lands.

Verification: unit tests for AEAD round-trip and KDF parameters; an injected-failure migration
test per step; a live devimint gate that starts the daemon encrypted, restarts it, and confirms
both ecash and a pending operation survive. Confirm on disk that the entropy is not recoverable
from the data directory alone.

title: Phase 7: encrypted app-state snapshot + restore drill (journal, ledger, registries, policy)
description:
Encrypted backup and tested restore of the wallet's app state — the journal, the operation ledger,
the federation registry, the candidate registry, and Policy.

ADR-0025 settled that the backup unit is the seed PLUS the joined federation IDs, and that the two
local stores carry no cross-store point-in-time guarantee: they are restored together from a single
snapshot or not at all. What the roadmap names as Phase 7 durability work, and what has no bead, is
the snapshot itself.

Why this is not merely nice-to-have: seed recovery rebuilds ecash balances, but it does NOT rebuild
send dedup state. The real-sats runbook says so directly. A host-disk loss today therefore recovers
the funds and loses the record of what was in flight — which is the precondition for a double-pay on
an in-flight send, not just a cosmetic history gap. It also loses the candidate registry, so
probe-gated funding decisions start from zero.

Required:
1. A single consistent snapshot across BOTH stores. Per ADR-0025 a mismatched pair is out of
   contract, so the snapshot must be atomic with respect to the actor rather than two independent
   file copies taken microseconds apart.
2. Encrypted at rest with the same AEAD discipline as the seed work; a backup that leaks the ledger
   leaks the user's entire payment history even if it holds no spending key.
3. A RESTORE DRILL, not just a backup writer. The gate is: kill the host, restore from the snapshot
   plus the seed, and confirm balances, ledger, registry, and in-flight operations all come back
   consistent. A backup nobody has restored is a hypothesis.
4. Specify what happens when the snapshot is OLDER than the seed's on-chain reality — restore must
   reconcile rather than trust the snapshot blindly.

Depends on the seed-at-rest encryption bead only for its AEAD/key-source machinery; if that is not
yet ratified, this bead may carry its own and note the coupling. Do not build a second key
management scheme.

Deliberately NOT in scope: remote/offsite backup transport, scheduling policy, or retention. Local
encrypted snapshot + restore drill first; where the file goes is an operator decision.

title: Policy: enforce an aggregate wallet exposure ceiling, not just per-federation
description:
`Policy` enforces `per_fed_cap` only. The real-sats pilot runbook states the consequence plainly:
"There is no aggregate ceiling in code — the total exposure a policy permits is therefore
`per_fed_cap x (number of joined federations)`."

So the ceiling an operator believes they set is not the ceiling the code enforces, and it rises
every time a federation is joined. The pilot survives this because `auto_join=false` keeps joins
manual and the federation count at two — but discovery-driven auto-join is a shipped capability
(Phase 5.1), and the moment it is turned on the wallet's total permitted exposure grows without
anyone editing a policy value.

Required:
1. A `total_cap` (msat) on `Policy`, enforced wherever `per_fed_cap` is enforced today, so a
   funding move that would push the WALLET total over the ceiling is refused with an explicit
   reason in `wallet-cli history` — not silently sized down to zero.
2. Refuse the policy itself when `total_cap < per_fed_cap`, which is an operator error that would
   otherwise make every move unfundable with a confusing per-move refusal.
3. Decide and document the interaction with joins: does exceeding `total_cap` block a JOIN, or only
   block FUNDING a joined federation? Recommend the latter — joining is free and reversible,
   funding is the exposure — but state it rather than leaving it emergent.
4. Update the runbook paragraph that currently documents the absence of this control.

Sizing note: this is a small, well-bounded policy change touching a daemon in production. It is not
urgent while `auto_join` stays false; it becomes urgent the moment it does not. Do not bundle it
with unrelated Policy work.

title: wallet-web: nix package, service unit, and operator runbook (dedicated origin, proxy, rotation, exposure limits)
description:
Package and document `wallet-web` for deployment. Today `flake.nix` exports packages for `walletd`
and `wallet-cli` only — the sidecar builds in the workspace but is not a deliverable — and the
real-sats pilot runbook covers the daemon exclusively.

`br-4yz` gates the sidecar on devimint. Nothing gates it on being operable.

Required:
1. A nix package + `mainProgram` for `wallet-web`, alongside the existing two.
2. A systemd unit (or the k8s equivalent matching how walletd is actually deployed), including the
   restart semantics: a sidecar restart revokes every session by design, so that is a documented
   feature, not an incident.
3. THE DEDICATED-ORIGIN REQUIREMENT, documented as unsupported-if-violated. Plan section 6c.1 says
   co-hosting the wallet under a path on a shared origin "must be documented as such": no cookie
   attribute, SameSite setting, or Origin check isolates two apps on one origin — the neighbour can
   fetch authenticated pages, read the CSRF field out of the HTML, and submit actions.
4. The `public_origin`-behind-a-TLS-proxy recipe. The sidecar terminates no TLS and never derives
   the origin from `Host` or `X-Forwarded-Proto`, so the proxy layout has exactly one correct
   configuration and several that fail closed in ways that look like a broken app.
5. The lost-password path: remove the config and re-run `wallet-web init`. Document what that
   RESETS — notably that init writes a complete config, so a tightened session timeout returns to
   its ceiling — and that it does not touch the daemon's token or the seed.
6. Password and daemon-token rotation procedures.
7. The exposure restriction, stated once and stated hard: loopback or a trusted overlay only. No
   public internet until seed-at-rest encryption lands. ADR-0028's Consequences section makes this
   the condition; this bead is where an operator actually reads it.

Depends on the auth work landing (there is nothing to run before then) but does NOT depend on the
full 6c surface — the operational shape is knowable as soon as login exists.

title: Release: re-canary production against the evacuation fee-cap release
description:
Re-run the production canary checklist against the release that carries the evacuation fee-cap fix.

The bead graph currently models canarying as a one-time terminal event: `br-prod-canary-nab` gates
"v1 pilot achieved" against RC b5f46de and has no successor. But the evacuation fee-cap work changes
a MONEY PATH on a daemon already holding real sats. Devimint proves protocol correctness, not
production gateway/guardian/network/deploy reality — which is the entire reason the canary bead
exists — and that argument does not stop applying just because the first canary passed.

Required:
1. Re-run the canary checklist against the exact release carrying the fee-cap change, not against a
   rebuild of it: receive, pay, scheduled top-up, standby funding, cross-fed move, daemon restart,
   reconcile, health monitoring.
2. Additionally exercise the changed path itself. A real evacuation is hard to stage on purpose —
   at minimum confirm on production data that the newly computed evacuation fee cap admits a
   full-balance drain of each pilot federation at current gateway prices, rather than only that
   nothing else regressed.
3. Do NOT raise the balance ceiling as part of this. Same amounts, same feds, new binary.
4. Destructive recovery testing stays on a separate sacrificial seed, as before.

OPERATIONAL/EXTERNAL — needs real production federations; cannot be drained in-repo. This is a
watch item with a checklist, not code work.

Standing rule this bead exists to encode: any change to a money path gets its own canary pass before
the ceiling moves. If a later bead changes another money path, clone this one.

title: Evacuate fee cap (1/3): Policy knobs + validation + propagation, no enforcement
description:
Add the two evacuation fee-cap knobs to `Policy` and thread them to every consumer. NOTHING READS
THEM FOR ENFORCEMENT YET — that is the next bead. This one is deliberately behaviour-neutral.

PARENT: `br-y2j` holds the full derivation, the worked numeric cases, the rejected alternatives and
the complete AC list. Read it. This bead carries sections **3, 3b and 3b-bis** verbatim; where this
text and `br-y2j` differ, `br-y2j` wins.

Why it is split out: `br-y2j` touches wallet-core, wallet-api, wallet-fedimint, wallet-cli, the
journal, the ledger, the move protocol and multi_client. Landing the plumbing first shrinks the
money-critical bead's file lock to the files that actually decide money, and this half is
independently deployable with zero evacuation-behaviour change.

## Required

1. `Policy` gains `evac_fee_base_msat` (default `200_000`) and `evac_fee_bps` (default `300`), each
   with a **NAMED** default function — `#[serde(default = "default_evac_fee_base_msat")]` and
   `#[serde(default = "default_evac_fee_bps")]`. A plain `#[serde(default)]` is a BUG on a numeric
   field: it yields ZERO, so a pre-change row decodes to `(0, 0)` — a zero cap under which nothing
   ever fits and every evacuation livelocks. The repo already has the correct pattern at
   `default_max_fee_bps_of_move` (`wallet-api/src/lib.rs:9`, used at `:32`).
   This is NOT a greenfield compatibility shim and must not be removed as one: the policy store is
   LIVE IN PRODUCTION, and the shipped operator procedure guarantees a release adding a policy field
   lets walletd start on the existing row (`docs/real-sats-pilot-runbook.md:321-326`). Dropping it
   means walletd fails to boot after this release.

2. VALIDATION. `evac_fee_bps` in `0..=10_000` with **0 allowed** (a base-only cap is legitimate);
   `evac_fee_base_msat` unrestricted. REJECT THE PAIR `(base 0, bps 0)` — it yields cap 0, nothing
   ever fits, and the result is the indefinite `Retryable` livelock the parent bead exists to kill,
   with no refusal at set time.

3. VALIDATE ON THE STANDALONE OVERRIDE PATH TOO, not only at `policy set`. `build_tick_policy`
   (`wallet-cli/src/main.rs:2283-2310`) layers tick/status overrides straight onto `TickPolicy`
   without calling `Policy::validate`, so `--standalone tick --evac-fee-base-msat 0
   --evac-fee-bps 0` would recreate the zero-cap livelock through a door the `policy set` check
   never sees.

4. PROPAGATION — name and update every surface: `wallet-api/src/lib.rs`,
   `wallet-fedimint/src/tick.rs`, `wallet-fedimint/src/service/mod.rs`, both CLI flag sets and their
   override paths (`wallet-cli/src/main.rs`), and `AllocatorSnapshot` (`wallet-core/src/types.rs:80`).

5. STALE COMMENTS in scope here because they describe the knobs: `AllocatorSnapshot.max_fee`'s "this
   bounds ONLY `Evacuate`" (`wallet-core/src/types.rs:92-94`) and the matching `Policy.max_fee`
   comment (`wallet-api/src/lib.rs:20-21`). Both become false. `allocator.rs:598-604`'s diagnostics
   comments and `max_fee_bps: None` recording belong to the NEXT bead, which changes what is
   recorded — do not touch them here.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `policy set` rejects `(base 0, bps 0)` and accepts `bps 0` with a non-zero base.
- [ ] The standalone override path rejects `(0, 0)` with the same cross-field error.
- [ ] A stored policy row with BOTH fields ABSENT decodes and yields the SHIPPED values — assert the
      values, not merely that it decodes.
- [ ] `evac_fee_bps` above `10_000` is rejected.
- [ ] Evacuation behaviour is UNCHANGED: an existing evacuation test passes untouched, and
      `Action::Evacuate` still carries `snapshot.max_fee`. Enforcement is the next bead.

## Note to reviewers
Fields that no enforcement path reads yet are INTENTIONAL here, not dead code. The enforcement bead
is a hard dependent of this one and lands immediately after. A finding that asks this bead to also
compute or apply the cap is asking it to become `br-y2j` again; decline it with this paragraph.

## Scope guard
Do not change `Action::Evacuate`, the executor, the sizing search, the ledger, or any fee arithmetic.
Do not touch `Move`. Do not update the runbook or README yet — the knobs do nothing until the next
bead, and documenting them as live would be false.
close_reason: Merged in PR #30 (7d5e69f). Policy gains evac_fee_base_msat/evac_fee_bps behind named serde defaults, validation rejecting the (0,0) pair and bps>10000 while allowing bps=0 alone, the same check on the standalone override path, and propagation to AllocatorSnapshot/TickPolicy/service/both CLI flag sets. Evacuation behaviour unchanged and PROVEN so: the golden fixtures pin the new knobs to values that disagree with max_fee, so accidental enforcement breaks every evacuation golden. Also corrected the max_fee docs, which claimed it bounds only Evacuate -- it is also the manual-verb default fee cap and the probe leg cap. rb-lite clean in 3 rounds, full 3-reviewer panel; fmt/clippy/742 tests green; CodeRabbit no actionable comments.

title: Evacuate fee cap (2/3): compute from executed net, persist across replay, non-monotone sizing
description:
THE MONEY CHANGE. Compute the evacuation cap as `base + proportional`, enforce it against the
EXECUTED net, make it survive replay, and keep the sizing search from reintroducing the livelock.

PARENT: `br-y2j` holds the full derivation, the worked numeric cases, the pinned fixtures and the
rejected alternatives. **READ IT IN FULL BEFORE STARTING** — this bead is a pointer, not a
replacement. It carries sections **1, 1b, 2, 2b, 2c, 2d, 2e** and every AC in the parent EXCEPT
LEDGER AGREEMENT and the runbook/README criteria, which belong to bead 3/3.

Depends on the Policy bead (1/3): the `(base, bps)` knobs, their validation and their propagation to
`AllocatorSnapshot` already exist when this starts. Do not re-add them.

## The invariant this bead owns, stated once

**The fee cap that is enforced is `base + floor(executed_net * bps / 10_000)` — computed from what
actually moved, persisted so a crash cannot resurrect the planned-amount cap, and reachable by a
sizing search that does not assume monotonicity.** Every requirement below is that sentence.

The three ways to ship this and still be wrong, all of which pass a naive test suite:
1. Compute the cap from the PLANNED amount. Plan 75,000 sats, get clamped to 1,000, authorise a
   2,450-sat cap against a 230-sat entitlement.
2. Compute it correctly and fail to PERSIST it. Replay reconstructs `MoveParams.fee_cap` from the
   original plan (`executor.rs:264`) and `assemble_move_record` treats params as authoritative
   (`move_protocol.rs:297`, `:418`), so a receive commit plus cache loss restores the planned cap.
3. Make the sizing predicate monotone to satisfy the bisection. `cap(a) = base + bps*a` is NOT
   monotone; forcing it is not the fix, and the parent's 2c worked case shows a combined bisection
   discarding a comfortably feasible window and returning to the exact livelock this bead kills.

## Required — see the parent for the derivation of every number
1/1b. Cap arithmetic: `cap_msat = base_msat + floor(executed_net_msat * bps / 10_000)`. FLOOR, in
  u128 or checked u64, saturating not wrapping. THE CAP'S BASE IS THE EXECUTED NET — deliberately
  not the base the SDK charges on. Tests derive the CAP from net while deriving each CHARGED fee
  from its real SDK base.
2. `Evacuate.fee_cap` comes from that, not `snapshot.max_fee`. `Move` stays on `move_fee_cap(...)`.
2b. Components snapshotted onto `Action::Evacuate` by `decide()` and carried through
  `MovePlan`/`MoveParams`; the FINAL recomputed cap committed into the receive operation's
  `MoveMeta` as `Option<Msat>` with `#[serde(default)]`, absent meaning `None` and NOT a zero cap;
  reassembly PREFERS the `MoveMeta` cap over `params.fee_cap`. Also plumb `OpArtifact` and
  `op_artifact_from_meta`/backfill (`multi_client.rs:1226-1259`) or crash safety cannot pass.
  The rejected alternative — re-deriving from a live `Policy` at execution time — is rejected in the
  parent with reasons; do not revive it.
2c. Two-pass sizing, the efficiency check as a POST-check, and the structural-refusal diagnostic.
2d. WARN on an out-of-envelope advertised ppm; do NOT reject on it.
2e. `Action::Evacuate` is serde-persisted inside the durable `Intent`; the new components are
  optional/defaulted and a legacy intent RETAINS its stored absolute `fee_cap` rather than adopting
  current policy defaults.

## Acceptance criteria
Every AC in `br-y2j` except LEDGER AGREEMENT and the two documentation criteria. Reproduced here by
name so none is quietly dropped — the parent carries each one's fixture and its red-first argument:
- [ ] CLAMP SAFETY  - [ ] CRASH SAFETY  - [ ] ECONOMIC VIABILITY (the ~365-chunk fixture)
- [ ] efficiency check is a POST-check  - [ ] NOTE-COUNT DISCONTINUITY
- [ ] NON-MONOTONE SIZING, INCREASING REGIME  - [ ] NON-MONOTONE SIZING, DECREASING REGIME
- [ ] LIVELOCK / GENUINE REFUSAL  - [ ] SIZING NEVER EXCEEDS `desired`
- [ ] STRUCTURAL REFUSAL IS DIAGNOSABLE  - [ ] THE PPM WARNING FIRES, AND DOES NOT GATE
- [ ] CAP ARITHMETIC (exact-cap admitted, cap-plus-one-msat refused)
- [ ] base-fees-above-the-old-cap no longer livelock  - [ ] full-balance drain in ONE operation
- [ ] small evacuation admitted, percentage-only cap shown to fail it
- [ ] a fee exceeding base + proportional is still refused  - [ ] `Move` unchanged, asserted
- [ ] legacy-intent replay retains its stored absolute cap
- [ ] legacy-`MoveMeta` fixture (row encoded WITHOUT the field) decodes to `None`, falls back, completes

## Scope guard
Per the parent: the per-federation balance cap (ADR-0018) stands, the trigger and route are
unchanged, evacuation does not become uncapped, and the absolute `max_fee` stays for the manual money
verbs. The `#[serde(default)]` allowance is the only KIND of compatibility concession. Ledger
truthing and the runbook/README updates are bead 3/3 — do not pull them forward, and do not leave
them undone either.

## Money-adjacent process
Dual adversarial review and a live devimint gate before this merges. No partial production deploy:
this bead is atomic with respect to the invariant above.

title: Evacuate fee cap (3/3): ledger reports the enforced cap and executed amount; runbook + README
description:
Make the ledger report the cap it actually enforced, and update the operator-facing docs.

PARENT: `br-y2j`. This bead carries sections **3c and 4**, plus the LEDGER AGREEMENT acceptance
criterion and the two documentation criteria.

Depends on the enforcement bead (2/3): there is no "final recomputed cap" to stamp until it exists.

## The problem

`FeeBreakdown.fee_cap` is stamped once from `Intent.max_fee` at plan time
(`wallet-core/src/executor.rs:54`, `journal.rs:2974-2978`), and `refresh_from_move` copies op-ids,
gateway and quoted fees but NOT `fee_cap` (`journal.rs:2987-3014`). So: plan 75,000 sats and the row
shows a 2,450-sat cap; clamp to 1,000 sats and the ENFORCED cap is 230 sats; the row keeps reporting
2,450 for its entire life. A post-incident fee audit against `wallet-cli history` therefore validates
fees the enforced cap would have refused — the ledger vouches for something that never happened.

## Required

1. Stamp the final recomputed cap onto the ledger row via `refresh_from_move`.
2. **AND the final AMOUNT with it.** `kind_from_action` seeds the row's amount from the PLANNED
   action (`wallet-core/src/ledger.rs:243`) and `refresh_from_move` does not copy `MoveRecord.amount`
   (`journal.rs:2984`). Refreshing only the cap yields a row reading `amount = 75,000 sats,
   fee_cap = 230 sats` — internally false, because an auditor recomputing from the displayed amount
   derives 2,450. Refresh BOTH or the fix makes the row worse, not better.
3. Update `README.md`'s policy-knob section and `docs/real-sats-pilot-runbook.md` §4 so the suggested
   `policy set` includes the new knobs, and state plainly that the absolute `--max-fee` NO LONGER
   BOUNDS AN EVACUATION. An operator who keeps tuning `--max-fee` expecting it to bound evacuations
   is the person this sentence exists for.
4. ADR-0029 is the authority and the implementation conforms to it. Only NON-SEMANTIC
   synchronisation is in scope — a status line, a code reference. A semantic change to the cap shape,
   route ordering or `Move` behaviour requires a separate decision BEFORE implementation, never an
   ADR edit that makes the document match the code.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] LEDGER AGREEMENT: after a clamp, the ledger row's `fee_cap` equals the ENFORCED cap AND its
      `amount` equals the EXECUTED amount — asserted after an ordinary clamp AND again after
      cache-loss reconstruction.
- [ ] The runbook's suggested policy includes the new knobs and states that `--max-fee` no longer
      bounds an evacuation.
- [ ] README's policy-knob section describes the evacuation cap's shape and who each cap governs.

## Scope guard
Read/report only. No change to the cap arithmetic, the sizing search, the persistence path or any
money decision — all of that is bead 2/3 and is already merged when this starts. If this bead finds
itself needing to change enforcement, that is a defect in 2/3 and belongs there.

title: Pin the delivered-net cap basis at the pre-mint gate and the executor recompute (driven fixture + TestRoute::with_recv_fed_fee)
description:
Pin the delivered-net cap basis at the two production sites a unit fixture cannot reach, and give
`TestRoute` the builder that makes the distinction constructible at all.

WHY THIS EXISTS: `br-evac-cap-enforce-vn6` established that every evacuation fee cap is computed
from the DELIVERED net (`invoice - receive_quote`), never from the sized ask. That invariant is
pinned by unit tests at the search's two admission seams and by direct `fits_cap` /
`combined_verdict` tests. It is NOT pinned at two production sites, and the code says so rather
than pretending otherwise:

1. the PRE-MINT gate (`wallet-fedimint/src/executor.rs`, the cap + viability checks immediately
   before `mc.receive`), and
2. the executor's post-receive RECOMPUTE, which commits the enforced cap into `MoveMeta`.

Both need a fixture that drives `drive_intent_step` against a mocked multi-client. Neither is
reachable from a pure quote-stream fixture.

THE BLOCKER UNDERNEATH: `TestRoute` initialises the receive federation fee to `|_| Msat(0)` and
exposes only `with_send_fed_fee`. With a zero receive fed fee the gross-up always solves exactly,
so **no composed async fixture in the suite can produce `delivered != ask` at all**. Until that
builder exists, every async test is blind to the very distinction the bead established. Add
`with_recv_fed_fee` (a step function, mirroring `with_send_fed_fee`) first; it is the enabling
change for everything else here.

WHAT THE LIVE GATE DOES AND DOES NOT SHOW: the two-federation devimint evacuation gate passes and
proves the path executes end to end including a hair-under delivery. It CANNOT distinguish the
delivered-net basis from the ask basis: in that fixture the two caps differ by 2 msat (213_499 vs
213_497) while the real fee has ~199_287 msat of headroom under either. Do not cite it as
evidence of the basis. It also never enters the refusal diagnostics at all, since it drives a
SUCCESSFUL evacuation.

Required:

1. `TestRoute::with_recv_fed_fee`, so a fixture can force a verified hair-under settle.

2. TWO SEPARATE DRIVEN CASES. They may share a fixture builder but they are DIFFERENT EXECUTIONS
   and must not be written as one test. A refusal commits nothing, so it cannot also produce a
   committed `MoveMeta` to inspect; an earlier draft of this bead asked for exactly that and a
   reviewer caught that it was impossible to satisfy.

   2a. REFUSAL, at the pre-mint gate. Assert the gate refuses on the DELIVERED net before
       `mc.receive` is called, with zero receive operations committed.

       THE DRIVEN VALUE IS `grossed.receive_quote`, not a receive-only `quoted_fee` or any other
       fee number. The production gate is
       `fee::total_within_cap(grossed.receive_quote, Msat(0), cap_rule.at(requote_delivered))`
       (`wallet-fedimint/src/executor.rs`), so a fixture that drives some other quantity never
       exercises the gate at all and proves nothing. Name the exact input in the test.

       THE QUOTE MUST SIT IN THE BAND, or the fixture proves nothing: `grossed.receive_quote`
       strictly ABOVE `cap.at(delivered)` AND at or BELOW `cap.at(sized_ask)`. A quote merely over
       the delivered cap is also over the ask cap once it is far enough out, so a gate STILL
       reading the ask refuses the same case and the test passes green against the very bug it was
       written for. Assert both bounds and state the two cap values as literals so the band is
       visible. Red-first against a gate reading the sized ask.

   2b. SUCCESSFUL SETTLEMENT, driven independently. Drive a hair-under settle to completion and
       assert the committed `MoveMeta.fee_cap` equals `cap.at(delivered)`, not `cap.at(sized_ask)`.
       This case must reach the post-receive recompute, so it cannot reuse 2a's refusing quote.

3. Re-point the two stale references that named `br-4yz` for this work — `DRIVE.md` and the
   comment in `wallet-fedimint/src/executor.rs` — at this bead. `br-4yz` is the wallet-web route
   manifest bead and has nothing to do with the evacuation executor; a reviewer caught the
   misattribution, and the risk is a maintainer believing this debt has an owner when it does not.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (all must be checkable, not asserted in prose):
- `TestRoute::with_recv_fed_fee` exists and a fixture using it produces `delivered != ask`.
- 2a: `mc.receive` is never called and no receive operation is committed; the driven value is
  `grossed.receive_quote`; both band bounds are asserted as literals; the test is red against a
  gate reading the sized ask.
- 2b: a committed `MoveMeta` exists and its `fee_cap` equals `cap.at(delivered)`; the test is red

- 2a and 2b are separate `#[tokio::test]` functions.
- No reference ASSIGNS this work to `br-4yz`: `br-evac-cap-driven-basis-v07` appears at both
  ownership sites it previously occupied. Do NOT check this as "zero occurrences of br-4yz" — that
  is unsatisfiable and destructive. `DRIVE.md` legitimately names `br-4yz` twice: once in the

NOTE ON THE EXISTING SEAM TESTS, so a future edit does not silently weaken them: their coverage is
a property of the PAIR, not of either test alone. `pass_one_revalidates_its_final_requote` pins the
settled amount 449_999; drift that deletes the pass-1 admission entirely would still satisfy that

title: Evacuation: a structural refusal cannot be released by any operator action
description:
A structural evacuation refusal is a LIVELOCK the operator has no lever against. The refusal
diagnostic added by `br-evac-cap-enforce-vn6` correctly identifies the condition and now says
plainly that a policy change will not release it — this bead is the missing mechanism that would.

THE CHAIN, verified end to end:

1. The refusal returns `ExecError::Retryable` (`wallet-fedimint/src/executor.rs`), deliberately:
   ADR-0029 forbids terminalizing, because that would strand a dying federation's balance.
2. The intent therefore stays `Pending` (`wallet-core/src/executor.rs`, the `Retryable` arm).
3. Reconcile reports `retryable > 0`, and watch SKIPS the tick entirely
   (`wallet-fedimint/src/runtime.rs`, `WatchReconcileOutcome::Ran(summary) if summary.retryable > 0`).
4. So `decide()` never runs again, and no new `Action` is ever created.
5. The pending `Action` carries the `(base, bps)` pair `decide()` admitted it with
   (`wallet-core/src/types.rs`, `fee_cap_components`), and the executor recomputes the cap from
   THOSE — not from current policy.

Consequently raising `evac_fee_base_msat` / `evac_fee_bps` has NO effect on the stranded
evacuation. There is no retry limit, nothing terminalizes a retryable intent, and no
cancel/abandon subcommand exists — the CLI has none. For a STRUCTURAL refusal (the fixed component
exceeds the cap base, so no amount fits at the admitted parameters) the intent retries forever.

WHY THIS IS P1: the funds are on a federation the wallet believes is shutting down. The operator
is told there is a structural refusal, changes the only knob the system exposes, and nothing
happens — while believing the problem is fixed.

Required: a SAFE pre-artifact replacement path. Safe means it may only run while nothing has been
minted or committed for that intent — the same window the pre-mint gate already establishes. It
must be idempotent, must not resurrect an intent whose receive has committed, and must leave the
ledger able to explain what happened.

Pin it END TO END: refusal -> policy change -> a FRESH action decided under the new parameters,
asserting the new cap is the one enforced. A unit test on the replacement call alone does not
demonstrate the livelock is broken.

DO NOT weaken step 1 as the fix. Terminalizing a retryable evacuation is what ADR-0029 forbids and
would strand exactly the balance evacuation exists to sweep.

title: watch: one retryable intent suppresses ticks for every federation
description:
`watch` skips the tick whenever reconcile reports ANY retryable pending work:

    WatchReconcileOutcome::Ran(summary) if summary.retryable > 0 => SkippedPendingRetry

`summary.retryable` is a GLOBAL count across every intent, so one federation's stuck retryable
move suppresses ticks for ALL federations — including healthy ones that have nothing to do with
it, and including the tick that would decide a fresh evacuation for a DIFFERENT dying federation.

Combined with `br-n8o` (a structural evacuation refusal retries forever, since nothing
terminalizes a retryable intent and no cancel path exists), this is not merely a delay: one
permanently-refusing evacuation halts the allocator's decision loop indefinitely, wallet-wide.

The skip itself is deliberate and its stated reason is sound — running the tick with unknown
pending-move state risks re-issuing a still-`Pending` prior-occurrence move under a fresh
occurrence, i.e. duplicate intents. The defect is the BLAST RADIUS, not the caution.

Required: scope the suppression to what is actually at risk. The likely shape is per-federation
(or per-intent-key) rather than a single global counter, so a stuck intent on fed A cannot
suppress decisions for fed B. Whatever shape is chosen must still prevent the duplicate-intent
case the current guard exists for.

Pin it: a fixture with a permanently retryable intent on one federation must still allow a tick to
decide for another, AND must still not re-issue the stuck one under a fresh occurrence. Both
halves, or the fix trades one defect for the one it replaced.
